World.title: Tanzania: Govt Announces Two-Month Illegal Firearms Amnesty
World.content:
Dodoma — THE government has announced a two-month amnesty for people possessing firearms illegally, giving them an opportunity to voluntarily surrender the weapons without facing prosecution.

The amnesty, which takes effect on September 1 and runs through October 31, this year, is part of a national campaign aimed at removing illegal firearms from communities and preventing their use in crime.

Minister for Home Affairs Patrobas Katambi said yesterday in Dodoma that the government had formally announced the amnesty through a government notice dated August 28, this year, as it seeks to strengthen peace and security in Tanzania.

Under the arrangement, people who surrender firearms they possess without the required permits or through unlawful means will not be prosecuted for the illegal possession.



Mr Katambi urged all people who possess firearms unlawfully or outside established legal procedures to take advantage of the opportunity and surrender the weapons.

He said the surrender exercise will be conducted at police stations, local government offices and ward executive offices, making it easier for illegal firearm holders to hand over the weapons without fear of prosecution during the amnesty period.

The minister, however, issued a strong warning to anyone who continues to possess an illegal firearm after the amnesty expires on October 31.

"Anyone found with a firearm after this amnesty period ends will have committed an offence and will face legal action as quickly as possible,"

Mr Katambi said, warning that continued possession would indicate malicious intent inconsistent with efforts to maintain a safe and peaceful nation.

The campaign is being implemented by the Tanzania Police Force in collaboration with other security and defence organs and will run throughout September and October. It will also involve the media and other key stakeholders in raising public awareness.

Inspector General of Police (IGP) Camillus Wambura said the amnesty was a deliberate government intervention designed to complement, rather than replace, police operations against illegal firearms.

"This campaign is not a substitute for police operations, but an additional tool to prevent these firearms from being used before crime occurs and before harm is caused," Mr Wambura said.

The IGP said Tanzania had continued to ratify and implement various regional and international agreements while strengthening its legal and operational systems for controlling the possession, use and distribution of firearms.

World.title: Libya: Can the African Union Remain Relevant in Libya?
World.content:
analysis

Unless the AU can help coordinate implementation of existing peace initiatives, its influence on the ground may continue to wane.

Fifteen years after the 2011 uprising that toppled Muammar Gaddafi, Libya remains fragmented. Rival eastern and western power centres prevent total collapse but block meaningful national reconciliation, institutional unification and democratic transition.

Instability fuels arms trafficking, organised crime, irregular migration, terrorism and foreign fighter movements across the Sahel and beyond. With Africa's largest oil reserves and about 150 armed groups, competition for resources exacerbates the crisis.

Libya has long been one of the African Union's (AU) most important files. The Peace and Security Council (PSC) has held at least 20 meetings on Libya since February 2011, and the AU High-Level Committee on Libya is the organisation's main vehicle for an African-led settlement.



In Libya's crowded mediation landscape, the AU stands out for its distinctive role in reconciliation. But can it use this position to align existing initiatives and ensure their implementation?

Recent developments suggest cautious but significant diplomatic progress in Libya. In January, the Presidential Council and the Government of National Unity in the west of the country signed the Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation. Other groups had signed in February 2025 after the AU facilitated the charter.

Other advances this year are the 11 April approval by rival administrations of the country's first unified budget in more than a decade. In another first, a joint military exercise facilitated by the United States in March brought together top rival commanders.

On 30 August, adversaries agreed on a 'landmark' roadmap to national elections within two years, mediated by the UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL). This follows a parallel, largely Libyan-led tripartite agreement signed on 16 June, which commits the parties to simultaneous presidential and parliamentary elections by 17 February 2027, establishes a sovereign oversight committee, and outlines steps to end the transition.

AU Commission Chairperson Mahamoud Ali Youssouf welcomed the June agreement as a step towards constitutional order and reconciliation. By contrast, UN Secretary-General Special Representative Hanna Tetteh didn't mention it in her 18 June remarks, instead prioritising the UNSMIL facilitate- roadmap.

In addition to Libya's overlapping peace processes, security and other concerns remain. At its 9 June meeting, the PSC reiterated calls for all foreign forces and mercenaries to withdraw and expressed concern over continued violations of the United Nations (UN) embargo, illicit fuel exports, armed clashes and deteriorating humanitarian conditions of African migrants in detention centres.

It recognised that Libya's core challenge was not a lack of peace efforts, but a persistent failure to implement existing agreements - at least nine major roadmaps or accords have been launched since 2011.

Libya's accords consistently collapse or stall at implementation. As the Tripoli-based Sadeq Institute's Anas El Gomati told ISS Today, 'Endorsement is not implementation.' The core obstacles are institutional and economic. Rival authorities in the east and west benefit politically and financially from maintaining parallel institutions - particularly through controlling oil revenues and state resources.

Oil revenues sustain competing security structures, administrations, judicial bodies and financial networks. El Gomati says elections won't resolve the crisis without deeper institution-building, public finance and security reforms.

External actors add to the complexity. El Gomati says the United Arab Emirates has faced little consequence or mediation attention despite being the primary external military patron of Khalifa Haftar's eastern-aligned Libyan National Army (LNA) since 2016. LNA-controlled territories also reportedly serve as a supply corridor for Sudan's Rapid Support Forces.

The PSC has rejected the presence of foreign forces, mercenaries and fighters. However, the 5+5 Joint Military Commission, comprising military negotiators representing both east and west, says fragmented security sector institutions hamper external force withdrawals.

In this environment, overlapping peace initiatives - the UN roadmap, AU efforts and the tripartite agreement - risk duplication and forum-shopping. Greater coordination is essential to turn recent diplomatic momentum into lasting impact.

Implementation of the AU's 2011 roadmap and high-level committee decisions has been slow due to external factors (foreign interference and competing mediation tracks) and internal constraints (limited follow-up capacity and resources, and competing continental priorities).

Nevertheless, a clear example of the AU's added value is the 2025 National Reconciliation Charter. The initiative brings together opposing power centres, has helped bridge Libya's political and geographical divide, and has contributed to diplomatic momentum. Unlike other actors in Libya focused on elections and institutions, the AU frames the crisis as both political and societal and prioritises national reconciliation, transitional justice and social cohesion.

The AU also collaborated with Africa's three UN Security Council members and the United Kingdom (as Libya's penholder) to secure the unanimous April 2026 adoption of Resolution 2819, which extended Libya's sanctions regime.

Close 

But unless the AU can help harmonise the implementation of existing peace initiatives, its influence on the ground may continue to wane.

The PSC should help coordinate action on the tripartite agreement, the UN roadmap and the reconciliation charter. This would reduce duplication and advance institutional reunification and the conduct of credible elections by the end of 2027. The PSC should also expedite its field mission to Libya and the relocation of the AU Liaison Office from Tunis to Tripoli, as agreed by the AU in 2022.

The AU's relevance in Libya will depend not on new initiatives, but on its ability to act as coordinator and guarantor of implementation in a landscape dominated by powerful external players and fragmented domestic interests.

This article was first published in the ISS PSC Report.

For permission to re-publish ISS Today articles, please email us. In South Africa, News24 has exclusive rights to republish ISS Today articles. In Nigeria, Premium Times has exclusive rights to republish ISS Today articles.

Zenge Simakoloyi, Research Officer, Africa Peace and Security Governance, ISS

World.title: Africa: The Drylands Dividend - the Smart Investment for Powering a Water-Scarce World
World.content:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Sep 1 2026 (IPS) - Open a can of something fizzy and the reason the sugar doesn't separate immediately is gum arabic, tapped by hand from acacia trees across the Sahel. Spray on perfume and the reason the scent is still there at dinner is frankincense, a resin cut from Boswellia trees on the dry escarpments of the Horn of Africa. The fat that gives a chocolate bar its snap may well be shea, gathered and pressed by women in the parkland belt of West Africa. The cashmere jumper came from goats that can only be raised on cold, dry rangelands.

These are drylands. They cover 44 per cent of the planet's land, hold 44 per cent of the world's cropland and half its livestock, and two billion people live in them. We have spent decades describing them as empty or unproductive. For a long list of things most of us use without thinking, they are the only places on earth that produce them at all.

It is no secret that our world is becoming hotter and drier. Three quarters of the planet's land experienced drier conditions in the last 30 years than the previous 30. This year's El Niño is intensifying fast, compelling the world to look back at what dryland systems already know. Nearly every model now points to a record-strength event: the US Climate Prediction Center puts the odds of a "very strong" El Niño at over 90 per cent for this fall and winter, and a 69 per cent chance it exceeds anything on record since 1950.

Drylands have been living through exactly this kind of shock-and-recovery cycle for generations, and their playbook offers real lessons. Farmers in places that have always been able to count on rain are beginning to face a question that dryland farmers answered generations ago: what do you grow, and how, when the water is not guaranteed?



Dryland systems are the longest-running operating record anywhere of producing value under conditions of scarcity, volatility and shock. These landscapes are home to generations of knowledge on how to thrive with limited water and high variability. This includes practices such as spreading risk across several crops and animals rather than betting the season on one, understanding land closely enough to move livestock before the pressure is too much, and building income that arrives at different times of the year so a bad month is not a ruined one. These are powerful lessons needed now.

Now is the time to listen and learn from dryland communities, practices, and regenerative production models. When this wisdom, data, and experience serve as our foundation, we can transition to sustainable business models and unlock investments to power our future world using knowledge that already exists in the places we have been calling marginal.

Mongolia, the host of the recently concluded UN's COP17 talks under the Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), is a case in point. Three quarters of Mongolia's land is already classified as degraded or at risk. However, Mongolian herders supply 40 per cent of the world's raw cashmere, increasingly innovating to shift away from an extractive model to practices that generate diverse value, from wool to grass-fed meat, examples of what a healthy landscape can offer.

In northern Ghana, the Ojoba Women's Shea Cooperative processes shea butter by hand in the arid Upper East Region, using a skill passed down through generations. They now supply international buyers including L'Occitane and Lush.

In both instances, the land already had value, and the skills already existed within the communities. What was missing was a route to the market willing to pay for them. These initiatives demonstrate what is possible when investment is designed around the realities and value in drylands.

Investment can take many forms: from financing cooperatives through the shift to new practices; insurance that pays out on rainfall; water and energy infrastructure that keeps a harvest sellable in extreme heat. There is growth potential beyond raw commodities too; processing into oils, powders, waxes compounds the returns. And payments for ecosystem services, from stored carbon, biodiversity and watershed protection, sit alongside that.

Donors like the European Union have already recognised the value of drylands with the €20 million Thrivelands initiative, led by Landscape Alliance, to build the coalitions and action this work needs; including innovations needed to protect and restore land. These innovations range from the tools to monitor and restore soil health accurately to the Land Degradation Surveillance Framework and the Regreening Africa app, which brings this data into the hands of farmers.

But public funding alone cannot unlock the drylands opportunities. Adapting to a drier world means restoring a broken nature finance system and closing the $700 billion finance gap to apply proven expertise across a growing area.

Many companies already depend on drylands through what they source, without having assessed how much of their supply comes from them. For those in the agrifood, textiles, and cosmetics sectors, investing in restoring and protecting these landscapes is a way to stabilise their supply chains, manage growing levels of risk and meet climate goals.

Close 

There is also the question of what inaction costs. Investing in drylands agriculture could avert a 12 per cent reduction in global food production over the next 25 years and prevent the release of about 60 per cent of stored carbon.

COP17 is a reminder of how little time is left. The UNCCD finance framework closes in 2030, with 82 per cent of the cumulative need for finance unmet. Time is running out to leverage the lessons from drylands to protect future food security. The gap between what is needed and what is being invested remains enormous.

The landscapes on which our future depends may be getting drier, but they are not devoid of opportunity. With science and innovation that enhances traditional knowledge, they are saturated with opportunities to bolster food security and climate resilience.

Dr Éliane Ubalijoro, chief executive officer of Landscape Alliance; Salina Abraham, Head of Thrivelands, Landscape Alliance

World.title: Uganda: Tooro Kingdom At Crossroads Over Succession
World.content:
Fort Portal, Uganda — The Tooro Kingdom is at a crossroads as some questions arise over the choice of the heir to King Oyo Kabamab Iguru Rukiidi IV, who passed away last Thursday in the United States where he was undergoing medical treatment.

The death has sparked a debate about the future of the kingdom's leadership amid conflicting information about the existence of a successor.

In an official statement, the Prime Minister of Tooro, Calvin Armstrong Rwomire, announced that the late King Oyo left behind a son who could potentially inherit the throne.

President Yoweri Museveni also echoed this claim, stating that the Queen Mother had informed him of the child's existence.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

However, this revelation has been met with skepticism by some royal insiders.

Charles Kamurasi, the Omusunga or head of the Tooro Royal Clan, expressed doubts about the story of the heir. Having known King Oyo since childhood, Kamurasi says he was surprised by the announcement of a son and questioned its authenticity.

He says the claim might be fabricated and emphasized that if no clear heir emerges, the succession should follow traditional lineage, specifically reserving the throne now for the lineage Rukidi III.

In an effort to manage the transition, a 21-member committee comprising elders from the Babiito clan has been established to oversee the traditional succession process. Led by Musuga Charles Kamurasi, the committee includes prominent Babiito elders such as Dr. Isaac Mayombo, Fr Dr. Charles Oyo, Dr. Kagoro Kaijamurubi, Job Karamagi, and Gilbert Mujogya.

The committee is tasked with planning and executting the kingdom's next steps to find a new ruler.

Kasaija Ernest Kusemerera, who is in charge of the Omukama's local security (Omukumirizi), says that as the kingdom awaits clarity, the focus remains on ensuring that the succession process respects tradition and maintains stability within the Tooro monarchy.

David Baguma, one of the ritualists at the Tooro Kingdom, states that if King Oyo's son indeed exists, his grandfather on the mother's side must first present him to the Babiito clan elders. Following this, the clan heads would conduct specific traditional rituals to prepare the heir for his future role before any formal procedures for his succession are undertaken.

Baguma emphasized the importance of maintaining calm during this uncertain period. He reassured the public that even if no clear heir emerges, the kingdom remains a well-established institution with clear protocols and structures to determine the next ruler.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 1, 2026
World.content:
Kenya Aviation Workers Call Off Strike, Resume Duties

Kenya's aviation workers have called off their strike and resumed normal duties after reaching a return-to-work agreement with employers. The deal provides for the immediate remittance of agency fees owed to the Kenya Aviation Workers Union and clears the way for fresh negotiations with the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority over a new collective bargaining agreement. The union has raised concerns about new pay guidelines issued by the Salaries and Remuneration Commission but will seek to address them through the negotiations. The agreement also covers a long-running recognition dispute between KAWU and Jambojet, which will be resolved through the courts. Workers who took part in the strike will be protected from victimisation, intimidation or disciplinary action. Both sides have committed to resolving future disputes through negotiations and established mechanisms.

Namibia Rejects US Health Data-Sharing Proposal



Namibia has rejected a United States proposal involving the sharing of health data and biological specimens, citing concerns that the agreement could undermine the country's sovereignty, privacy laws and control over its biological resources. The dispute has complicated negotiations over more than N$730 million in potential funding for the country's HIV and tuberculosis programmes. The US said that the proposed agreement would only involve aggregate rather than personally identifiable data. Namibia is exploring alternative funding options to ensure the continued delivery of essential HIV services if a mutually acceptable agreement cannot be reached.

Gabon Victims Demand Accountability a Decade After Post-Election Violence

A decade after violence erupted following former president Ali Bongo's disputed re-election in Gabon, survivors and relatives of those killed are still demanding the truth and accountability. The unrest began after Bongo was declared the winner of the 2016 election. Security forces launched an assault on opposition leader Jean Ping's headquarters, marking the beginning of several days of unrest, looting and violent repression. The true death toll remains unknown. Survivors are now calling for a full investigation. Questions persist over the possible involvement of French nationals and whether French authorities fully cooperated with investigations into allegations of crimes against humanity.

South African Airline Defends Low Flypast Over Cape Town Stadium

South African airline Airlink has defended a dramatic low-altitude flypast involving two aircraft over Cape Town's packed DHL Stadium before the Springboks' rugby match against New Zealand. Flight tracking analysis suggested the lead aircraft passed less than 50 feet above the top of the stadium, prompting criticism and concerns about the risks of the manoeuvre. However, Airlink said the stunt was carefully planned and approved by aviation authorities, with highly experienced crews after rehearsing safety and speed limits. Many South Africans have praised the pilots' precision and skill.

Close 

Niger Uprising Exposes Cracks in Military, Russia Ties

Niger's failed military uprising has exposed deepening frustration within the armed forces, where many soldiers face poor pay, inadequate equipment and dangerous conditions while battling persistent Islamist insurgencies. The unrest has also raised questions about the stability of President Abdourahamane Tchiani's military government and its reliance on Russia's Africa Corps, which reportedly helped suppress the uprising. Analysts said that the events highlight underlying structural problems within Niger's military. They said that Russian support may help stabilise the junta in the short term without addressing the grievances and security challenges threatening its long-term survival.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Zimbabweans Abroad Raise Alarm Over Political, Economic and Human Rights Crisis
World.content:
Zimbabweans living abroad have raised fresh concerns over worsening political, economic and human rights conditions in the country, warning that mounting pressures are increasingly forcing citizens to seek opportunities and sanctuary outside Zimbabwe.

The civic movement Citizens Watch Zimbabwe, based in South Africa, has called for urgent action on issues ranging from constitutional changes and the rule of law to the high cost of passports and the decline in public services.

The movement held a media briefing in Johannesburg on Saturday.

Key issues on the agenda included human rights, the rule of law, governance, economic hardship, public service delivery and challenges facing Zimbabweans in the diaspora.



Speaking on the sidelines of a delayed press conference, the movement's president, Patience Chard, said Zimbabweans were increasingly feeling that their rights were being eroded and that Government needed to listen to their concerns.

"The reason why we've gathered here is because the Zimbabweans are going through a lot of difficulties here and back home. So, we're here to speak about all these things. Maybe the government can hear us when we gather together in our numbers. We've got issues of passports. Our passports, their prices are ridiculous.

"And we also got a challenge of our constitution that was recently amended. And that was the main reason why we formed our organisation because of the constitution, we are against the president. Because our rights have been violated as citizens. So that means we no longer Zimbabweans. If we cannot vote, what is the reason for us being Zimbabweans if we can't vote."

The movement has also criticised Zimbabwe's 2030 Agenda, describing it as unconstitutional and arguing that it does not reflect the views and concerns of ordinary Zimbabweans on the ground.

Channel Africa

World.title: Kenya: Aviation Workers Call Off Strike After Deal On Pay, Union Dues
World.content:
Nairobi — Aviation workers have called off their industrial action and resumed normal duties after reaching a return-to-work agreement with their employers, ending a standoff that threatened to disrupt operations in the aviation sector.

The agreement provides for the immediate remittance of agency fees owed to the Kenya Aviation Workers Union (KAWU) and currently held by the Kenya Airports Authority (KAA).

The deal also clears the way for fresh negotiations between KAWU and the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA) over a new Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), after the Salaries and Remuneration Commission (SRC) withdrew its earlier guidance on the negotiations.

Under the agreement, KAWU and KCAA will proceed with CBA negotiations immediately, with the authority committing to honour and implement the outcome of the talks.



The SRC had withdrawn its initial guidance contained in a July 28, 2026 letter and issued new parameters on September 1 to guide the negotiations.

KAWU, however, said it had reservations about the new SRC parameters and would seek to address what it considers shortcomings during the CBA negotiations.

The agreement marks a significant shift in the dispute, with the union opting to end the strike in exchange for commitments on the outstanding issues.

"While the union has reservations on the SRC guidelines issued on the 1st September, 2026 ... and seeks to remedy the shortcomings arising from the said advisory during the CBA negotiations," the agreement states.

The parties also reached an understanding on the long-running recognition dispute between KAWU and Jambojet.

The matter is currently before the courts, and the parties agreed to await the court's determination and abide by the eventual decision.

Jambojet also committed to complying with all applicable legal and procedural requirements relating to trade union recognition.

With the agreement executed, KAWU formally called off the industrial action and directed affected workers to resume their normal duties immediately.

The workers are expected to cooperate with management to restore and maintain normal operations.

The agreement also contains a non-victimisation clause, shielding employees who participated in the industrial action from reprisals.

Under the clause, no employee shall be victimised, intimidated, discriminated against or subjected to disciplinary action because of their participation in the strike.

The parties further committed themselves to maintaining industrial peace and resolving any outstanding disputes through consultation, negotiations and established dispute-resolution mechanisms.

Close 

The agreement effectively shifts the battle from industrial action to the negotiating table, particularly over the terms of the KAWU-KCAA CBA.

The outcome of those negotiations could determine whether the concessions secured by the union translate into improved terms for aviation workers, amid continued scrutiny of how public-sector remuneration is guided by SRC parameters.

World.title: South Africa: Limpopo Village Cut Off as Bridge Collapses - South African News Briefs - September 1, 2026
World.content:
Limpopo Village Cut Off After Makeshift Bridge Collapses

The community of Mafarafara village in Limpopo has once again been cut off from a nearby clinic after a makeshift bridge across the Tubatse River collapsed following recent heavy rains, reports EWN. The bridge, built from wooden logs, sticks and corrugated iron sheets, provided a vital but unsafe link between remote villages. Residents must now either swim across the swollen river or pay more than R100 for transport to and from the clinic.

Hawks Officer Questioned Over R3 Million Cash Deposits

The Madlanga Commission has questioned KwaZulu-Natal Hawks Lieutenant-Colonel Deenadayalan Govender over more than R3 million in cash deposits made into his bank accounts between August 2022 and December 2023, reports SABC News. The commission said that the deposits far exceeded his monthly take-home salary. He is being investigated to determine whether the movement of the funds could indicate possible money laundering. Govender has also faced questions about his relationships with tow-truck businessman Clive Naicker and convicted drug dealer Timmy Marimuthu.

Cape Town Signs Cheaper Solar Power Deals

Cape Town has signed two solar power purchase agreements that will add 70 megawatts of electricity from plants in Atlantis and Philippi to the city's grid at prices below Eskom's tariffs, reports EWN. The city said that the future price increases will be linked to inflation rather than Eskom's tariff hikes. This might potentially help to limit electricity costs for residents. Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis said the 20-year contracts are expected to provide R8 billion worth of electricity and reduce the city's reliance on Eskom.

World.title: Massive World Trade Center steel beam arrives at West Point, uniting 9/11 heroes with generation sent to war
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A 21-foot steel beam recovered from the South Tower of the World Trade Center arrived at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point Tuesday, bringing a physical piece of the Sept. 11 attacks to the institution that trained generations of Army officers who would go on to serve in the wars that followed.

The 16,900-pound beam was brought to West Point as part of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation’s Steel Across America tour, a nationwide commemoration marking the 25th anniversary of the attacks. Tuesday’s ceremony was the tour’s 33rd stop.

West Point Superintendent Lt. Gen. James B. Bartholomees III said the steel connects the courage shown by first responders on 9/11 with the Americans who answered the call to serve in the years that followed.

"As we approach the 25th anniversary of 9/11, this piece of steel reminds us of the courage of first responders like Stephen Siller and the countless Americans who answered the call in the years that followed, including generations of West Point graduates," Bartholomees said. "Today, young men and women continue that legacy of service, guided by Duty, Honor, Country."

9/11 STEEL BEAM ARRIVES AT FLORIDA SCHOOL WHERE BUSH LEARNED AMERICA WAS UNDER ATTACK

The ceremony brought together cadets, faculty, staff and guests and opened with a color guard and Pipes & Drums procession by members of the NYPD, FDNY and Port Authority Police Department. The program also included the national anthem, an invocation and blessing of the steel, and a moment of reflection accompanied by "Amazing Grace."

BENJAMIN HALL TACKLES GRUELING ONE WORLD TRADE CENTER CLIMB ON PROSTHETIC LEGS TO HONOR FALLEN HEROES

Frank Siller, chairman and CEO of Tunnel to Towers and the brother of fallen FDNY firefighter Stephen Siller, recalled his brother’s final actions on Sept. 11.

"Twenty-five years ago, my brother Stephen strapped on 60 pounds of gear and ran through the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel toward danger, duty, and the people who needed him inside those towers," Siller said.

9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS

"Duty, Honor, Country: those values connect West Point cadets, Stephen, and first responders all across this country," he continued. "We are grateful to West Point for welcoming us, and we leave more committed than ever to making sure the sacrifice of September 11 is never forgotten."

According to Tunnel to Towers, Stephen Siller was off duty when the attacks began and ran through the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel carrying 60 pounds of gear toward the World Trade Center, where he died while responding to the attacks.

FOX NATION, TUNNEL TO TOWERS EXPLORES HOW AMERICA’S PASTIME HELPED A GRIEVING NEW YORK HEAL AFTER 9/11

The foundation created in his memory provides mortgage-free homes to Gold Star and fallen first responder families with young children, builds specially adapted smart homes for catastrophically injured veterans and first responders, and works to address veteran homelessness.

For some of those gathered around the beam Tuesday, its arrival at West Point carried a personal connection between the first responders who rushed toward the towers and the service members who deployed overseas in the years that followed.

9/11 MUSEUM TO OFFER FREE ADMISSION FOR VETERANS AHEAD OF MEMORIAL DAY WEEKEND

Col. Dan Steuwe of the U.S. Army recalled an image that he said many soldiers in his platoon carried with them after 9/11 as they went overseas.

"There was a cartoon character that a lot of the soldiers in my platoon carried with us after 9-11 as we went overseas," Steuwe said. "It was one of the firemen handing off the American flag to a service member coming out of the rubble of the towers."

Steuwe described the image as another symbol of the unity between first responders and service members "serving something greater than ourselves and protecting this country."

Kelly Heffner, who is listed by Tunnel to Towers along with her husband, Tom Heffner, as a supporter and corporate sponsor, became emotional after approaching the South Tower beam.

"To touch that beam, there’s an energy with it and it brings you back and it — you know that you can never forget," Heffner said.

The artifact's stop at West Point comes nearly 25 years after the attacks sent a generation of American service members to Afghanistan, Iraq and other theaters during the war on terror.

9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

Bartholomees later joined Siller to receive a commemorative steel flag on behalf of West Point. The custom-built piece features the New York City skyline and Twin Towers and incorporates World Trade Center steel. According to Tunnel to Towers, the flag is presented to people and institutions that have demonstrated a commitment to the foundation’s mission.

After the formal program, attendees were invited to approach the beam and spend time reflecting beside the steel.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Steel Across America tour is scheduled to continue Thursday at the Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston.

World.title: Self-funded CEO claims GOP nomination to challenge Massachusetts Democrat’s second-term bid
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Former medical device executive Mike Minogue won the Massachusetts gubernatorial primary Tuesday, defeating Brian Shortsleeve, a former executive at the MBTA, the state-run transit agency.

The winner will now face favored Democratic Gov. Maura Healey, who is running for a second term. Massachusetts has had continuous Democratic representation in Congress since 1996, but Republicans have had considerably more success in races for the governor's mansion since the Reagan era.

Minogue emphasized his business credentials in campaign materials, citing his work at GE Healthcare before leading Danvers-based Abiomed.

GOP GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE FIGHTING TO FLIP BLUE STATE UNVEILS HEALTHCARE PLAN TO LOWER COSTS, EXPAND ACCESS

Minogue said that, while he was at Abiomed, the company developed the world’s smallest heart pump and doubled the size of its headquarters, increasing its in-state capabilities and creating jobs.

Minogue also drew attention on social media when Boston-based Canadian American investor Kevin O’Leary, better known as Shark Tank’s "Mr. Wonderful," appeared in one of his videos and said he does not usually "show for politicians."

"Massachusetts is ‘dead-money’ now. We need a guy like this to run the show," O’Leary said in July.

TRUMP KEEPS WINNING REPUBLICAN PRIMARIES; HIS LOSSES MAY BE MORE REVEALING

According to The Boston Herald, Healey launched a last-minute ad attacking Minogue as "MAGA Mike," which the newspaper said shows the executive "has Healey’s attention" and may help Shortsleeve.

Minogue won the state’s GOP convention endorsement with 70% of the vote, while Shortsleeve earned his ballot position with a fraction of a percentage point more than the required 15%, according to reports.

Minogue self-funded roughly $7 million of the more than $7.5 million he raised in the first quarter, hosted a fundraiser with Vice President JD Vance and has donated to Trump and the RNC. Shortsleeve raised about $646,500 in the first quarter of 2026.

Healey was formally renominated Tuesday after running unopposed. Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll, a fellow Democrat, also advances unopposed to the November election.

Republicans, however, have no candidates in about half of the state’s congressional districts or in the races for secretary of state and state auditor. A signature problem has forced lieutenant gubernatorial candidate Anne Manning Martin to run a write-in campaign.

The district in the Berkshires, the district covering much of the Massachusetts Turnpike corridor, and two exurban Boston-area districts to the north and west have no Republican candidates competing Tuesday, guaranteeing Democratic nominees will advance in those races ahead of November.

Massachusetts state government has not always been as reliably Democratic in modern times despite the conditions in this year’s contests.

Former Gov. Charlie Baker, a moderate Republican, preceded Healey from 2015 to 2023.

Former Sen. Mitt Romney, R-Utah, served as Massachusetts governor from 2003 to 2007 and opted against re-election before launching an unsuccessful presidential bid against President Barack Obama.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Romney was preceded by several Republican governors. From 1997 through the end of Romney’s tenure, Republicans continuously held the governor’s office.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Former libertarian presidential candidate Gov. William Weld, former Gov. Paul Cellucci and former Gov. Jane Swift were consecutive Republican governors. Swift was elevated to the office when Cellucci became then-President George W. Bush's ambassador to Canada.

Weld was preceded by 1988 Democratic presidential nominee Gov. Michael Dukakis, and Democrats more often held the governor’s office in the preceding era.

World.title: 80-year-old Dem beats back generational challenge after going all-in on trans athletes
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

One of the only Democrats stumping for transgender rights on the campaign trail fought back a younger challenger pushing generational change in the Senate.

Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., withstood a challenge from Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., to again be crowned as Massachusetts’ Democratic nominee for Senate in his quest for a third full term on Tuesday night. The Associated Press projected Markey would defeat Moulton less than an hour after polls closed.

Markey, who has represented Massachusetts in Congress for nearly five decades, survived Moulton’s campaign focused on generational change by leaning into his progressive bona fides. Notably, he is one of the few Democrats running this midterm cycle who is continuing to push for transgender rights, particularly in sports.

TOP 5 MOST HEATED MOMENTS AS PROGRESSIVES SPAR OVER WHO IS FURTHER TO THE LEFT IN FINAL DEM SENATE DEBATE

"Trans athletes should be able to play," Markey told The New York Times. "That reflects Massachusetts and who we are. And Seth Moulton does not."

The position, which has been used by Republicans as a political rallying cry on the campaign trail and one that Democrats have largely remained quiet about as they push to flip both chambers of Congress, is one that Moulton argued played a major factor in Democrats’ losing across the board in 2024.

"I have two little girls, I don’t want them getting run over on a playing field by a male or formerly male athlete, but as a Democrat I’m supposed to be afraid to say that," Moulton said at the time.

DEMOCRATS STAY QUIET ON NEXT STEPS AFTER SUPREME COURT TRANSGENDER SPORTS RULING

Given Massachusetts’ position as a deep-blue bastion — the Bay State hasn’t had a Republican senator since 2013; former Sen. Scott Brown lost to Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass. — it’s unlikely that Markey’s position will cost him in November.

And his primary victory marks another win for progressives. Markey, who co-authored the Green New Deal resolution years ago, boasted the backing of progressive titans, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.

WATCH: LAWMAKERS REVEAL WHERE THEY STAND ON CONGRESSIONAL TERM LIMITS AFTER RECENT HEALTH SCARES

It also serves as a blow to a broader push among Democrats across the country looking for generational change, particularly after the tumult that followed former President Joe Biden and his attempt to run for a second term in the White House.

Though longtime incumbents have been defeated, including Rep. John Larson, D-Conn., 78, by the much younger Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin, 47, Markey was able to hold on despite Moulton making age a key factor in his campaign.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Markey’s victory over Moulton isn’t the first time that a younger candidate has stepped into the arena only to be felled by the octogenarian.

Markey bested Massachusetts political royalty in 2020, beating former Rep. Joe Kennedy III in a primary contest that, like his contentious battle against Moulton, centered on a changing of the guard in the upper chamber.

World.title: Travelers warned of murder, kidnappings and drink-spiking robberies in vacation hot spot
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Americans heading to Brazil are being warned to watch their drinks, stay alert at ATMs and avoid certain areas after U.S. officials recently flagged an array of safety risks.

The State Department updated its Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution advisory for Brazil Aug. 31, though officials noted the country's advisory level remained unchanged.

The main reasons for the advisory update are "crime and kidnapping," officials said.

TERROR THREAT LOOMS OVER COASTAL DESTINATION AS US WARNS ATTACKS COULD STRIKE WITHOUT NOTICE

The advisory also warns that, in Brazil, violent crime "occurs in urban areas, day and night. Crimes include murder, armed robbery and carjacking."

The State Department also said criminals target foreigners through dating apps or at bars before drugging and robbing them.

"Assaults are common, including with sedatives or drugs placed in drinks, especially in Rio de Janeiro," the advisory said.

ROBBERIES, ASSAULTS AND RAPES SPUR NEW US TRAVEL WARNING FOR POPULAR CARIBBEAN GETAWAY

U.S. officials also maintain a Level 4 Do Not Travel warning for certain areas, including international land borders, informal housing developments and certain areas surrounding the capital of Brasília.

Kidnapping for ransom involving U.S. citizens is rare but occasionally occurs, according to the State Department.

"Brazilians are most often targeted, but foreigners remain vulnerable," the advisory said.

CLICK HERE TO 

"Express kidnapping — in which criminals force victims at gunpoint to withdraw cash from multiple ATMs or transfer funds via banking apps (commonly Pix) — is an ongoing threat to both locals and foreigners."

Travelers are advised to stay aware of their surroundings, avoid displaying signs of wealth and use caution at night, particularly at beaches, bars, transportation centers and on public transit.

Officials also recommend watching drinks closely, avoiding food or drinks from strangers and remaining alert to potential online dating scams.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Be careful at major transportation centers or on public transport, especially at night," the advisory added. "Passengers are at higher risk of robbery or assault when using public buses in Brazil."

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for additional comment.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Brazil advisory comes amid other recent State Department warnings for Americans traveling abroad.

For example, officials are urging Americans traveling to Israel to reconsider their plans and to remain alert as security conditions can change quickly.

The State Department also warned Americans to exercise increased caution in Ecuador due to violent crime, terrorism and kidnapping.

World.title: Germany blames Russia after explosive-laden drone found near Ukrainian cargo planes at major airport
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Germany has accused Russia of carrying out a failed drone sabotage operation at Leipzig/Halle Airport and announced Tuesday it would close Russian diplomatic facilities, escalating tensions after investigators linked Moscow to last month's attack.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Russia's consulate in Bonn will be closed and the contract for the Russian House cultural center in Berlin will be terminated after German authorities concluded Moscow was behind the Aug. 4 incident.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said forensic evidence and intelligence findings tied Russia to the attack, in which authorities found a drone carrying an explosive device beside a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

Officials said the explosive failed to detonate because of a faulty detonator.

Germany also said it believes a second drone collided with a nearby cargo aircraft, while officials have linked the incident to what Dobrindt described as Russia's "well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe."

US INTEL WARNS RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH LIMITED ATTACK ON NATO ALLY IN EFFORT TO FRAGMENT ORGANIZATION: REPORT

Russia has denied the allegations.

The Russian Embassy in Berlin called the accusation "absurd," while Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said Moscow would respond in a "mirror-image" fashion to Germany's actions. The embassy later described Berlin's measures as an "unprecedented escalation in Russian-German relations."

In addition to closing Russian diplomatic facilities, Wadephul announced tighter entry restrictions for Russian nationals and additional measures targeting Russia's shadow fleet. He also said he had summoned Russia's ambassador to Germany, Sergei Nechayev.

The announcement marks Germany's first public attribution of responsibility for the airport attack. Until now, Berlin had said only that "foreign powers" may have been involved, though U.S. media previously reported American officials believed Russia was responsible.

US ALLY ON PUTIN’S DOORSTEP BRACES FOR WAR AS RUSSIA TENSIONS TAKE OMINOUS TURN

Leipzig/Halle Airport is one of Europe's largest cargo hubs and serves as a logistics center for Germany's military and NATO allies. It is also home to Ukrainian Antonov transport aircraft, making it a strategically important hub supporting Ukraine's cargo operations.

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte backed Germany's findings, writing on X that the alliance "stands in full solidarity with Germany."

"The evidence is clear. And I welcome the measures announced by Germany in response," Rutte wrote.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the European Union was preparing additional sanctions against Russia, while Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk accused Moscow of escalating tensions across the region.

EUROPE BANKROLLS PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE EVEN AS NATO RACES TO BOLSTER DEFENSES

The developments come as Germany has warned it faces an increasing campaign of hybrid threats targeting military, transportation and critical infrastructure. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said last week those responsible for hostile acts against Germany would "pay a price."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

German police separately said Tuesday they were investigating improvised explosive and incendiary devices discovered at a power substation in the eastern state of Brandenburg after a damaged power line caused a temporary outage. Authorities have not identified who planted the devices.

"Wheel of Fortune" announcer Jim Thornton has been suspended.

Thornton was hired as an announcer for the game show in 2011.

The alleged incident was related to an American Airlines flight Thornton took in May, according to TMZ, in which another passenger complained about Thornton’s behavior. He was met by law enforcement at the gate.

TONY ROMO HIT WITH SEVERAL NEW CITATIONS AFTER OWI ARREST, FURTHER JEOPARDIZING RETURN TO NFL BROADCASTS

"On May 14, American Airlines Flight 1276 was met by law enforcement upon arrival at Los Angeles International Airport following concerns reported by a customer onboard," the airline told TMZ.

Thornton was not taken into custody, TMZ reported.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the airline for comment.

Thornton replaced iconic "Wheel of Fortune" announcer Charlie O’Donnell after O’Donnell's death in 2010.

BOB BARKER ALLEGATIONS IN EXPLOSIVE DOCUSERIES WERE 'TRUE AND THEN SOME,' FORMER GAME SHOW HOST SAYS

Before joining "Wheel of Fortune" and "Celebrity Wheel of Fortune," he did voices for shows like "Celebrity Death Match," "The Cleveland Show" and Pixar’s "Monsters, Inc."

He has also worked on "The Price is Right" and "Jeopardy!" And he’s worked for KNX 1070 Newsradio since 1985.

World.title: Rams star Puka Nacua faces new abuse allegations as $150 million payday hangs in balance
World.content:
Puka Nacua was on track to become the NFL’s next $150 million receiver until his offseason went sideways, with new abuse allegations surfacing as the league reviews his conduct.

Nacua’s ex-girlfriend and the mother of his child, Hallie Aiono, has now accused him of abuse and neglect during their four-year relationship.

Aiono made the claims in a TikTok video and then took it down.

"I went from loving somebody so deeply for four years, I felt it in my bones, to experiencing extreme betrayal, abuse, complete neglect from them, in what felt like it happened almost overnight," Aiono said.

She said the private turmoil had taken a greater toll than their public disputes.

"A lot of the things that were public affected my mental health," Aiono said.

"But honestly, the things that were happening in private are what completely crushed me and altered my brain chemistry. Those parts, what people never saw or knew of, are what broke me."

The latest allegations add to a disastrous offseason for the fourth-year receiver, who led the NFL with 129 catches and added 1,715 receiving yards last season.

KANSAS CITY CHIEFS WIDE RECEIVER RASHEE RICE IS ON PACE FOR AN ALL-TIME FUMBLING OF THE BAG

In March, Nacua was named in a civil lawsuit filed by Madison Atiabi following a chaotic New Year’s Eve party.

The filing accused him of biting Atiabi’s shoulder, biting another woman’s thumb and directing an anti-Semitic slur at a guest. Nacua’s attorney, Levi McCathern, strongly denied the allegations and characterized the legal action as an extortion attempt.

"Puka denies these allegations in the strongest possible terms," McCathern said. "Our office was contacted with demands of millions of dollars in exchange for not publicizing these allegations. This is not a legitimate claim. It is blackmail."

NFL PUTS 'INSPIRE CHANGE' AND 'CHOOSE LOVE' ON FIELDS BUT NOT SO AGGRESSIVE ABOUT ITS DOMESTIC ABUSE ISSUES

McCathern also denied the alleged slur, saying a "completely sober witness" had stated that Nacua never made the comments. He characterized the alleged biting incidents as "horseplay."

Nacua voluntarily entered a Los Angeles rehabilitation facility in early March, before Atiabi’s allegations became public. His attorney said the program was intended to help him focus on his personal growth.

That off-field baggage is now bleeding into Nacua’s contract talks.

Nacua recently hired WIN Sports Group to negotiate a new deal, but the Rams reportedly do not expect to extend him before the season. The team appears prepared to wait for more clarity in his legal situation and evidence of sustained personal growth before handing him top-of-market money.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The NFL is also reviewing Nacua’s conduct under its Personal Conduct Policy , which allows the league to discipline players even when criminal charges are not filed.

Nacua’s production gives him leverage, but unresolved allegations and a potential suspension make a $150 million commitment a much tougher sell for the Rams.

Rep. Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass., is officially the Democratic nominee for Massachusetts' 7th Congressional District after facing no challengers in Tuesday's primary.

But despite controversies involving Pressley's personal finances, her husband and racially charged remarks she's made, the "Squad member" will face no Republican candidate in the November general election.

Pressley's district encompasses roughly three-quarters of Boston, and the Cook Political Report ranks it as Solid Democrat. She was first elected to office in 2018, alongside Squad members Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich.

Although Pressley faced no competition in the primary or general election, she joined other Democratic candidates on the campaign trail, including state Rep. Tram Nguyen, a Democratic candidate for District 6. Like Pressley, Nguyen is calling to abolish ICE, implement Medicare for all and end all military aid to Israel.

ILHAN OMAR ON TRACK FOR FIFTH TERM AS MINNESOTA VOTERS MAINTAIN FAR-LEFT STREAK

With no challengers from either political party, Pressley continued criticizing President Donald Trump and the conservative-majority Supreme Court this election cycle.

Following the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, which held that creating a second majority-Black district constituted unconstitutional racial gerrymandering, Pressley accused the Trump administration of being "anti-Black" and "that would rather Black Americans pick cotton than pick the president, than pick their congressperson, than pick a senator."

MASSACHUSETTS SENATE CANDIDATES TRADE SHARP ATTACKS IN FIERY DEBATE AS INCUMBENT MARKEY SKIPS EVENT

A week before the primary, Pressley spoke at a campaign rally for Markey in which she said White supremacy is thriving under Trump's presidency.

VAN JONES WARNS FAR-LEFT SOCIALIST AGENDA IS 'REGRESSIVE' THREAT TO DEMOCRATIC PARTY

When introducing a bill in April aimed at providing relief to people facing eviction, Pressley called evictions "an act of violence."

In July, Pressley's husband, Conan Harris, also faced scrutiny after a company he partners with secured a $2 billion contract from the state to build a new courthouse in Massachusetts. World.title: Alaska finalizes Senate race for November: 3 Republicans — 2 Dans Sullivan — and 1 Democrat
World.content:
The Alaska Division of Elections on Tuesday named the four Senate candidates who will be on the ballot this fall in a closely watched race that will be decided by ranked-choice voting.

Voters will make their selections among two Republicans named Dan Sullivan, another named Gerald Heikes and Democrat Mary Peltola, who finished first during the all-party primary in which the top four advance to the general election.

Democrat David Leslie had finished fourth, but he withdrew from the race Monday. His withdrawal means fifth-place candidate Gerald Heikes, a Republican, will appear on the ballot.

Dan J. Sullivan and Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, R-Alaska. AP; Getty Images

The race is considered one of the most competitive in the 2026 cycle and a potential pickup for Democrats, who are hoping to gain control of the Senate. It’s made headlines due to the novelty of having two candidates with the same first and last name.

Dan J. Sullivan, a former schoolteacher who came in third in the primary, is seeking to unseat Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. But his candidacy has faced legal challenges from the senator and other Republicans who allege he is working with Peltola, a former congresswoman, and entered the race as a potential spoiler. He and Peltola have denied any coordination with each other, as have their campaigns.

Although the Alaska Supreme Court allowed Sullivan to stay on the ballot after originally being disqualified by the Division of Elections, state and federal authorities are conducting their own investigation into his campaign.

The Division of Elections on Tuesday also named general election candidates for the governor’s contest, including Republicans Dave Bronson and Bernadette Wilson and Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, the top finisher in the primary.

They are running to replace term-limited GOP Gov. Mike Dunleavy.

Tom Begich, a Democrat who finished second in the primary, withdrew from the race before Tuesday.

World.title: Whistleblower says USPS system Trump ordered for mail ballots is flawed and untested
World.content:
An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint this week that the technical system the U.S. Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed, untested and likely to cause major disruptions in this fall’s midterm elections if it is implemented.

President Donald Trump signed an executive order in March that directed his administration to create federal lists of citizens and asked the Postal Service to transmit mail ballots to only those people. A federal judge has blocked the order from going into effect amid ongoing litigation over its constitutionality; the whistleblower complaint highlights potential issues that could arise if the courts ultimately declare it lawful.

The USPS typically is responsible only for transporting mail ballots between election officials and voters, and the federal government has never kept a central list of all American citizens. Trump ordered the agency to take on an unprecedented and complex role in the process this year amid a broader attempt to exert greater control over the country’s elections and his continued unfounded claims of widespread voter fraud.

The technical system the USPS assembled to vet voters was developed in a “rushed, chaotic, and fundamentally flawed process,” according to a whistleblower complaint sent to the office of Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., a member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. Blumenthal sent the complaint to Postmaster General David Steiner on Monday, asking for more information.

“This administration seems hell-bent on changing the framework of casting ballots in this country, clearly for political reasons,” Blumenthal said on a call with reporters Monday. “It is unconstitutional, as is argued in the courts by the litigation that is ongoing, but this disclosure indicates that it is also blatantly incompetent and incapable of actually delivering ballots that are lawful in this midterm election.”

In a statement Tuesday, the White House disputed the whistleblower’s allegations.

“The process of building software to carry out this new verification check is neither complex nor unique for USPS since the Postal Service regularly uses bulk mailing and intelligent mail barcodes for a wide variety of large customers,” said Lauren Bis, a White House spokesperson.

The whistleblower is identified as an anonymous federal official who is being represented by Whistleblower Aid, a nonprofit group that represents public- and private-sector employees making such complaints. They allege that the USPS didn’t begin building its portal for verifying ballots “in earnest” until June, giving itself less than three months to complete a system that would ordinarily take at least nine to 12 months to build.

The agency last month finalized the rule for how it would implement the changes, which would create a massive new workload for election officials and put up hurdles for millions of voters to cast ballots by mail.

A spokesperson for the USPS said the agency had received Blumenthal’s letter and is “carefully reviewing the concerns he and the whistleblower have raised.”

“The United States Postal Service has spent months developing a U.S. Federal Ballot Mail Portal to provide election officials with a simple, secure, and efficient way to share lists of individuals receiving ballots by mail in their respective states,” the spokesperson said in a statement. “The portal is just one part of a broader, year-round effort by the Postal Service to ensure that election mail and ballots are handled and delivered securely, reliably, and efficiently.”

Large batches of ballots would be rejected by the portal if even a single ballot couldn’t be verified, the whistleblower said.

“As presently designed, if even one bar code on one single ballot in a bulk-mailing of 10,000 ballots fails to properly scan during the verification process, the entire batch is rejected and sent back to the state — effectively stopping the ballots from being mailed to voters,” the complaint reads. “Even under ordinary circumstances this would be problematic because of predictable errors in any barcode scanning process.”

The whistleblower said workers involved in developing the USPS system feared it would crash and described the process just days before the project was originally scheduled to be released to the public Tuesday as a “s--- show,” according to the complaint.

The whistleblower also said the USPS had ordered workers to continue developing its system, despite court orders blocking implementation of the project.

A federal court order Monday said the government could continue building its portal as long as the states aren’t required to participate.

World.title: No plans for ICE to be at polls for midterms, DHS says
World.content:
ICE officers have not received guidance telling them they need to do anything in addition to their regular duties on the day of November’s midterm elections, a senior Homeland Security official told NBC News.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said at a news conference Tuesday in New York that ICE officers will be at a polling place only if “there is a threat to that polling place” or if officers are serving a warrant on someone “that we have been actively tracking down.”

“ICE isn’t there to patrol the polling places,” Mullin said.

Asked whether ICE officers would enter polling places, Mullin said they would if they had warrants.

“If we’re serving a warrant, we will be where we need to be,” Mullin said.

President Donald Trump and Mullin have claimed without offering any evidence that there are over 250,000 noncitizens on voter rolls across several states. Mullin recently threatened state election officials with possible prison time if they didn’t comply with the administration’s methods to determine whether noncitizens were on their voter rolls. Several state officials have pushed back against sharing private state voter roll data that includes personal information, such as Social Security numbers.

World.title: Key Texas county votes to cut polling sites ahead of the midterms
World.content:
Officials in Texas’ third-largest county voted Tuesday to significantly reduce the number of polling sites for this fall’s midterm elections, drawing protests from Democrats and voting rights advocates.

Commissioners in Tarrant County, a fast-growing and politically competitive area that includes Fort Worth, approved a plan that results in 92 fewer Election Day polling locations compared with the 2022 midterms. The roughly 30% reduction leaves the county with 224 polling sites to serve 1.3 million voters. Voters in the county are able to cast ballots at any of those polling sites.

The three Republicans on the Tarrant County Commissioners Court voted for their plan, while the two Democrats voted against it.

Research has found that each additional minute of travel time to a polling location can affect voter participation. The NAACP, the American Civil Liberties Union of Texas and other groups said in a letter that the changes would hit voters of color hardest because many of the reductions are in majority-minority areas in Fort Worth and Arlington.

Supporters of the plan say that it will save money and that there are more than enough options for people to vote.

The move comes amid a critical Senate contest in Texas, with Democratic state Rep. James Talarico taking on state Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican.

Talarico urged the county to reject the plan ahead of Tuesday’s vote.

“The most powerful people in this county, the most powerful people in this country, don’t want us to be able to vote easily,” Talarico told reporters Sunday, according to The Associated Press.

Tarrant County has emerged as a key political battleground in Texas. President Donald Trump won it in the 2024 presidential race after Joe Biden flipped it four years prior. And Democrats Beto O’Rourke and Colin Allred narrowly carried the county in the 2018 and 2024 Senate races, respectively, even as they both went on to lose.

Texas law gives counties the power to decide how many polling sites they use. And some counties have begun using fewer sites as they have moved to countywide voting in recent years.

Dozens of voters urged the commissioners to vote against the cuts. Some criticized the elimination of specific polling places — like one at the University of Texas at Arlington — while others noted that the county has experienced significant population growth and voter participation in recent years.

“The right to vote is the bedrock of our democracy,” said a woman named Linda Northern. “This will make it harder for brown, Black and low-income voters to have the same right to vote as you do. This is wrong.”

Tarrant County Commissioner Roderick Miles Jr., a Democrat, added ahead of the vote, “This is about ensuring that the rights that people bled and died for are accessible to everybody.”

Tarrant County Judge Tim O’Hare, a Republican on the commissioner court, argued that Miles wanted more polling sites in his area.

“There’s no argument to that that you can come up with other than you want to be able to have more in your precinct,” O’Hare said.

A handful of speakers supported the plan, noting that some sites were used by few voters and required a significant number of poll workers and financial resources.

“I support the proposition that’s in front of us as far as reducing the number of voting sites. I’ve been a poll watcher, a poll worker, a precinct chair and all those things, and when you vote, when you go to a poll place that had 34 people all day long, you think this is kind of a waste of resources,” said one speaker, who did not identify herself.

World.title: Judge rules that the trial of Tyler Robinson in Charlie Kirk’s killing can go forward
World.content:
A judge in Utah on Tuesday ruled that a trial for the 23-year-old man accused of fatally shooting prominent conservative political activist Charlie Kirk can move forward.

District Judge Tony Graf issued the decision after a day of arguments in a probable cause hearing. Prosecutors argued there was enough evidence against Tyler Robinson to proceed with the case, while defense attorneys maintained that the evidence was insufficient.

Fourth District Court Judge Tony Graf speaks during closing arguments for the preliminary hearing for Tyler Robinson, on Tuesday. Francisco Kjolseth / The Salt Lake Tribune via AP

“It is hereby ordered that the defendant, Tyler James Robinson, is bound over for trial,” Graf said.

Robinson’s defense attorney then entered pleas of not guilty on all counts on his behalf. The next court date was set for Oct. 23.

Prosecutors have charged Robinson with aggravated murder, a first-degree felony that makes him eligible for the death penalty, and other counts.

Robinson is accused of killing Kirk with a single rifle round fired from a rooftop at an event at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10. The assassination of Kirk, the 31-year-old co-founder of the youth advocacy group Turning Point USA and a close ally of President Donald Trump, rocked U.S. politics.

Tyler Robinson at a hearing in Provo, Utah, on Dec. 11. Rick Egan / Pool via Getty Images file

In the lead-up to his ruling, Graf allowed lawyers on both sides to present closing arguments Tuesday. Evidence was presented in July.

“It’s not difficult to understand the motive here,” Utah County prosecutor Ryan McBride told the court during the state’s closing arguments. “The defendant’s views were repugnant to the positions that Charlie Kirk famously took.”

McBride alleged that Robinson threatened the lives of the people who attended Kirk’s event last September.

“You can’t shoot a rifle into a crowd of 3,000 people without knowing that you create a great risk of death to all those around your target,” McBride said in part.

Robinson’s defense attorney, Richard Novak, said the state can’t prove what would have motivated the shooting.

“There’s no evidence as to really what was in Mr. Robinson’s mind, if in fact he was the shooter, about Charlie Kirk,” Novak said.

“Because we have no testimony that Mr. Robinson had ever spoken about Charlie Kirk, that he’d ever heard anything he’d said, that he’d ever discussed anything” about Kirk in the past, Novak said.

Tyler Robinson, left, speaks with defense attorney Staci Visser as he attends a preliminary hearing in 4th District Court in Provo, on Tuesday. Francisco Kjolseth / The Salt Lake Tribune via AP

Another defense attorney, Staci Visser, argued that Utah’s legal aggravator that Robinson’s act posed a great risk of death to others does not apply because multiple shots or threats were not made.

“There is one act, there is one shot, there is one bullet, there is one victim,” she said.

Graf in his ruling allowed the aggravator and said the state met its burden at this preliminary stage, but he did not rule on the merits.

Tuesday’s high-stakes hearing came nearly two months after prosecutors laid out a detailed public reconstruction of the alleged events surrounding Kirk’s killing and presented a trove of evidence against Robinson, including security video, digital records and forensic material.

David Hull, a former State Bureau of Investigation agent, characterized Robinson’s alleged movements before and after the assassination. Hull’s testimony at a five-day hearing was accompanied by excerpts from campus video shown in court for the first time.

Fourth Judicial District Courthouse in Provo, Utah, before a key hearing for Tyler Robinson, who is accused in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk. Hannah Schoenbaum / AP

Robinson arrived at the university hours before the shooting, bought a meal from a campus Chick-fil-A restaurant and made contact with representatives for Turning Point USA, Hull testified. Robinson then changed outfits and took a position on a rooftop overlooking the amphitheater where Kirk was speaking, Hull said.

In a video shown in court July 7, Robinson could be seen crouching on the rooftop, Hull told the court. Then, after a bullet hit Kirk, Robinson could be seen darting across the roof, dropping to ground level and sprinting away on foot, Hull added.

Prosecutors played another video featuring partially redacted excerpts from law enforcement investigators’ interview with Lance Twiggs, Robinson’s former romantic partner and roommate.

The day after Kirk’s assassination, Twiggs told investigators, Robinson nervously paced their apartment and expressed regret. Twiggs told investigators that he asked Robinson whether it was true that he fatally shot Kirk.

In the emotional interaction that followed, according to Twiggs, Robinson “said he wishes he hadn’t done it.”

Twiggs told investigators that Robinson said he intended to confess to his parents or go to the police. He turned himself in to law enforcement authorities later that day.

Investigators have said they found the suspected murder weapon — a bolt-action rifle — wrapped in a towel in a wooded area near the Utah Valley University amphitheater. DNA from both Robinson and Twiggs was on the towel, Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina of the Utah Department of Public Safety testified July 7.

Robinson’s lawyers tried to throw doubt on the DNA evidence and pressed a defense witness, FBI forensic analyst Amanda Bakker, about the potential for error in forensic testing and other issues.

Robinson’s defense lawyers have not provided an alternative theory for who killed Kirk.

In a charging document filed last September, prosecutors highlighted inscriptions alleged to have been etched on each round of the rifle, including the phrases “Hey Fascist! Catch!” and “If you Read This, You are GAY.”

Twiggs, in the recorded interview played in court, told investigators that Robinson never talked about Kirk before the shooting. The roommates-turned-partners had originally bonded over their shared love of video games, Twiggs said.

Kirk family attorney Jeffrey Neiman asked that the court act swiftly and to “set this trial as soon as practically possible.”

“The United States Constitution guarantees criminal defendants many rights. The right to delay is not among them,” Neiman said.
