He was subsequently dismissed from service earlier this year.He then approached AFT principal bench not to challenge IAF's disciplinary right, but to request "dismissal" be changed to a "discharge" so he could seek future civilian employment.The bench held that while dismissal is warranted when rules are breached, exceptions must be considered in this case. "The respondents could have granted discharge to the applicant, but in the garb of maintaining discipline they dismissed him. The effect of both is identical inasmuch as the respondents do not want the service of the applicant."

World.title: U.S. strikes Iran and Tehran fires back as hostilities flare again
World.content:
The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), and Tehran fired missiles and drones in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war that has lasted more than six months.

The U.S. strikes followed others on Sunday that abruptly ended a month without military action and threatened to fully reignite a conflict that has spiked global oil prices and posed political problems for Republicans in November’s midterm congressional elections. The renewed fighting comes after President Donald Trump had appeared to pivot toward trying to bend Iran to his will through economic sanctions.

“If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings,” Mr. Trump warned on social media.

Today at 12 p.m. ET, U.S. forces began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran. The strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region. — U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) September 1, 2026

U.S. Central Command said the latest strikes were in response to Tehran trying to attack commercial ships and American forces in the Middle East. Trump offered an additional explanation, telling Fox News in a phone call that U.S. forces struck Iran’s radars.

“They tried to rebuild their radar because they can’t see anything,” Mr. Trump told Fox. “We waited until it was almost built and then we hit it.”

Iranian state media reported that the U.S. had bombed civilian sites along Iran’s southern coast and hit a civilian airport. A U.S. strike hit a home where a wedding ceremony was being held in Kuhestak in southern Iran, killing two people and wounding at least 20 others, Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province’s deputy governor, told Iranian state television in a phone call.

Iran’s Armed Forces General Staff and its joint military command said the armed forces would deliver what they described as “crushing and devastating blows” against the United States. The state-run IRNA news agency cited a statement by Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard, which warned that the attacks have only strengthened the Islamic Republic’s resolve and tightened Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of the world’s oil normally flows.

Explosions were reported across several southern Iranian coastal areas, including the port city of Bandar Abbas that is home to naval and air force facilities as well as Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Witnesses in Bandar Abbas told The Associated Press that the explosions were stronger than those on Sunday and said they saw smoke rising from the eastern part of the city on the strait.

Iranian state television said U.S. strikes hit a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island and several civilian sites in Hormozgan province. It said a fishing pier and a Ports and Maritime Organization tower in Sirik were among the locations struck.

State TV also reported that the U.S. military struck the civilian Jiroft Airport in central Iran’s Kerman province, saying a projectile struck an area outside the runway and caused no casualties or damage to airport infrastructure. U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment on those reports.

The U.S. and Iran are both seeking control over the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway off Iran’s coast that is a vital oil shipping corridor. Tehran effectively closed it after the war began.

Oil prices have moved sharply higher this week with renewed clashes between Iran and the United States. Crude, already up about 7% this week, continued to rise following the strikes on Tuesday.

The price of crude has jumped more than 50% this year and it’s dragged the cost of gasoline upward with it. The cost for a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. ticked higher again overnight to $4.10, according to AAA. Last year at this time, a gallon cost $3.19.

Before military action began again, the Trump administration had argued that hitting the right economic target in a campaign of financial isolation would get Tehran to its breaking point. Now, strikes are renewing even as U.S. stockpiles of advanced interceptors have been diminishing and the war has been unpopular among many Americans.

A return to open conflict would be dangerous for the region, where Iran has targeted U.S. military bases and infrastructure in Gulf countries since the war began.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said earlier Tuesday before the latest strikes that the Islamic Republic is ready to return to the interim ceasefire deal reached with the U.S. in June if Washington does the same.

“If the U.S. returns to its commitments in the memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately reciprocate,” Iranian state media cited Pezeshkian as saying at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan.

The June interim deal called for an immediate ceasefire and started a 60-day period for negotiations aimed at reaching a wider agreement, but crumbled soon afterward.

In the previous strikes on Sunday, U.S. Central Command said its forces struck Iranian rocket launchers that would launch sea mines into the strait.

Iran responded to Sunday’s attacks by launching missiles at U.S. sites in Jordan, which were intercepted, while United Arab Emirates said it stopped an Iranian drone over its waters. Trump acknowledged Monday that more strikes might be necessary.

The American military in recent days has cast the renewed fighting as limited, though Trump had acknowledged Monday that more strikes might be necessary.

U.S. Central Command said Monday on X that its attacks on Iranian targets on Sunday were narrowly focused.

“U. S. forces took limited, precise action against IRGC minelaying forces posing an imminent threat in the Strait of Hormuz,” U.S. Central Command said. “In essence, Iran created the threat and the U.S. military eliminated it to protect civilian mariners, commercial shipping, and the free flow of global commerce.”

Central Command reiterated Tuesday that its attacks followed Iranian aggression against commercial vessels and American troops in the region.

World.title: Nepal flash floods aftermath LIVE: Death toll crosses 1,000 as rescuers recover more bodies; nearly 4,000 still missing
World.content:
The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal surged to 1,050 on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), with security forces recovering more bodies from eight districts of the country, officials said. Nearly 4,000 people, including 583 foreigners and 83 security personnel, still remain missing the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said.

Watch | How a school in Nepal saved 900 students from a devastating flash flood

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah, meanwhile, said that the devastating flood that entered Rasuwa through the Bhotekoshi River bordering Tibet last week was due to climate change. Mr. Shah further said that climate change is a global contribution and disaster response remains a global responsibility.

The number of Indian nationals rescued in the wake of the devastating flash floods in Nepal stands at 163, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, as India sustained its relief and rescue efforts in coordination with Nepalese authorities. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also said a 19-member specialised forensics team from India that began functioning in Kathmandu on Sunday (August 30), as well as a tunnel rescue team deployed in Nepal in a statement shared along with the post.

World.title: Three candidates shortlisted for Ram Janmabhoomi Trust’s first CEO
World.content:
New Delhi

The search committee constituted to select the first Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust (SRJTKT) has shortlisted three candidates and submitted their names to the Trust, the committee said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).

The Trust, which oversees the Ram temple in Ayodhya, is expected to choose one of the three candidates at a meeting on Wednesday (September 2, 2026).

The decision to appoint a CEO came amid the controversy over alleged theft and irregularities in the handling of donations at the temple. Following the embezzlement allegations, SRJTKT general secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra resigned.

On July 6, the trust announced a major administrative overhaul, including the creation of the CEO post. The move was aimed at strengthening administrative oversight and restoring confidence in the trust’s functioning.

“The trust was also considering changes to its bylaws to formally provide for a CEO and clearly define supervisory responsibilities, particularly in relation to fund management,” a source close to the selection committee informed.

Selection process

To select the CEO, a three-member committee was formed comprising retired Justice Pramod Kohli, retired Lieutenant General V.K. Chaturvedi and scientist Dr. Suresh Haware.

The selection process began in July after the committee finalised the eligibility criteria, which included experience in temple administration and being a “staunch Hindu”. Applications were closed on July 18, following which online interviews were held in early August. Sixteen candidates were subsequently called to Ayodhya for in-person interactions on August 11 and 12.

“A total of 5,585 applications were screened using AI-assisted tools as well as manual review,” said search committee secretary Sameer Panda. The evaluation was conducted by teams based in Delhi-NCR, Pune and Sambalpur in Odisha, Mr. Panda said.

The names of the shortlisted candidates have not been disclosed, but sources said the panel includes candidates from government and private sectors. The three names have not been placed in any order of preference.

The committee’s final report was presented at a meeting attended by trust treasurer Swami Govind Dev Giri, Mahant Dinendra Das, acting general secretary Krishna Mohan and Ayodhya District Magistrate Shashank Tripathi.

World.title: CJP chief hails Supreme Court's quashing of FIRs against students
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) welcomed the Supreme Court's move to quash all FIRs registered against students who participated in the NEET protests across the country, calling it "absolute justice".

Talking to reporters here, Mr. Dipke thanked the court and said justice had been dispensed to all those who fought at Jantar Mantar and to the families of those who died do to NEET paper leak.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (September 1) quashed all First Information Reports (FIRs) registered against students who participated in the CJP-led protests between July 20 and 25 across the country. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant also directed the Centre to provide within three months compensation to families of students who ended their lives over the NEET paper leak.

"Our demands have been met. This is absolute justice. It took us a month [for this]," Mr. Dipke said.

He said this was made possible due to people's power, adding that he had been holding meetings with several delegations on the issue.

"I apologise to the families that we could not save your kids. We are very sorry that you lost your kids," the CJP convener said, referring to those who lost their loved ones and blamed the government for its failure.

The students lost their lives because of the government's failure, he alleged, and said the government had also accepted that it would provide compensation to the families of students who died.

"The government has accepted the demands, but it has to take responsibility that not a single student dies due to paper leak," the CJP convener said.

Mr. Dipke further added that the government must ensure that no student loses life due to failure of the system.

"We cannot afford this anymore," he said.

The CJP-led march on July 20 in Delhi saw clashes between protesters and security personnel, who used lathis and tear gas shells to disperse crowds attempting to move towards Parliament.

The student-led protests, which spread to several cities, were centred around the resignation of the then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The agitation, which began at Jantar Mantar on June 20, was called off on July 25 after Mr. Pradhan resigned and the government accepted the CJP's other demands.

World.title: World War II: The unsung role of India and its soldiers in the global conflict
World.content:
The years spanning the Second World War, from Germany’s invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, to Japan’s surrender on September 2, 1945, remain etched in history as a global conflict that lasted six years and involved millions of people across four continents. Approximately 85 million people lost their lives, most of them civilians, due to mass killings, genocide, starvation, and disease

World War II, which also bears the grim distinction of being the only conflict in which nuclear weapons were used, was fought between the Axis powers, principally Nazi Germany, Italy and Imperial Japan, and the Allied powers, including Great Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States, France and China.

Also read | When the world went to war

India’s forgotten history

In India, memories of the war have largely receded from public consciousness, as the years between 1939 and 1945 are remembered chiefly as the closing phase of the struggle for Independence.

Although the Indian Army fielded the largest volunteer force and fought on battlefields across Africa, Europe and Asia, there is little by way of a comprehensive archive documenting its experiences. Britain, the United States and France have fared better, with museums and archival institutions ensuring that the memories and lessons of war are preserved.

Also read | Remembering the war, reminiscing forgotten Indians

Between war and nationalism

India’s reticence towards the two World Wars stems from the uneasy relationship between its contribution to the fight against fascism abroad and the nationalist movement at home. The success of the former is often viewed as having come at the expense of the latter. The roots of this perception lie in the dashed expectations of greater autonomy after India supported Britain during the First World War.

Britain had already alienated many Indian nationalists through the imposition of martial law after the First World War, culminating in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919. Matters were further complicated when Viceroy Lord Linlithgow declared war on Germany on India’s behalf in 1939 without consulting Indian leaders. The situation became even more contentious when Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s Indian National Army aligned itself with the Axis powers in the belief that doing so could hasten India’s freedom.

India’s pivotal role in World War II

India raised the largest volunteer Army in history for the Second World War, with 2.5 million men serving. More than 87,000 of them are buried or commemorated in war cemeteries in India and abroad. Soldiers from undivided India were awarded 31 Victoria Crosses, accounting for about 15% of all such honours conferred during the conflict.

Also read | The guns at last light

Field Marshal Claude Auchinleck, Britain’s last Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army, acknowledged years later that without Indian soldiers, non-combatant labourers, material resources and financial support, the course of both World Wars might have been very different.

Beyond a distant war

More than 1,61,000 personnel laid down their lives in the two World Wars. Yet the prevailing perception is that these were wars fought for someone else and in distant lands. As a result, India’s substantial contribution has often been marginalised in historical narratives.

But these were not just European wars to defend foreign lands. During the Second World War, Japanese forces advanced through Burma, now Myanmar, posing a direct threat to India. Their advance was halted at the battles of Imphal and Kohima between March and July 1944.

Indians fought not only across South Asia but also in several parts of Africa, Europe and the West Asia. India also served as a crucial geographical barrier between Imperial Japan and Nazi Germany, preventing the two Axis powers from linking up through the West Asia. Maintaining this separation was vital to the success of the Allies in the war. Had Germany and Japan been able to coordinate their campaigns more closely and gain access to the oil resources of the West Asia, the balance of the war could have shifted dramatically in favour of the Axis powers.

Also read | Retracing Chennai’s role in the Second World War

World War II in Visakhapatnam

Although the Second World War began in Europe in 1939, by early 1942 it had spread deep into Asia as Japanese forces advanced through Malaya, Singapore and Burma (now Myanmar). British authorities feared that India’s eastern coastline could become vulnerable to attack. Visakhapatnam, with its harbour and strategic position along the east coast, quickly assumed military significance. Historian and chronicler Edward Paul, who has extensively documented the city’s wartime history, notes that fears of a Japanese occupation had a profound impact on both the administration and residents.

Those fears materialised on April 6, 1942. That morning, Cocanada, now Kakinada, was bombed by a lone single-engine aircraft, becoming the first town in India to be attacked from the air. Journalist, author and former Editor of The Hindu Mukund Padmanabhan records this in his 2024 book, The Great Flap of 1942: How the Raj Panicked Over a Japanese Non-invasion. Visakhapatnam was bombed three times on the same day and suffered far greater damage.

World.title: Congress attacks BJP over exclusion of over 2 crore voters in Maharashtra SIR
World.content:
Flagging the exclusion of 2.06 crore names in Maharashtra’s draft electoral rolls after the special intensive revision (SIR), the Congress on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) said votes were being added and deleted to ensure that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) wins elections.

The deletions in Maharashtra, where draft rolls were published on Monday (August 31), are the largest in absolute numbers for any State in the ongoing Phase 3 of the SIR.

Following the 2024 Maharashtra elections, the Congress had formally submitted representations to the Election Commission alleging large-scale voter roll manipulation, including unusual voter spikes in several constituencies. It had alleged that forged documentation, such as fake Aadhaar cards with mismatched names and photos, were used to add fictitious voters without physical verification of addresses.

On Tuesday (September 1, 2026), Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said “the BJP and the ‘vote theft commission’ keep changing their tactics, and they will continue to do so; the goal remains just one: BJP’s victory at any cost, and the end of India’s democracy”.

In a post on X, he said: “Maharashtra 2024 - Suddenly, 3.9 million new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft.”

“And now in Maharashtra, 2.07 crore voters have been removed from the draft list — that’s every fifth voter. Lok Sabha 2024: 9.29 crore, Vidhan Sabha 2024: 9.7 crore, SIR 2026: 7.78 crore. Which list was correct,” Mr. Gandhi asked.

“For a government built on vote theft, the people are not important—that’s why this BJP neither listens to the people nor obeys their command,” he added.

Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge said votes are added when it suits the BJP. “Where it doesn’t, votes are split to perpetrate vote theft,” he said.

“The BJP’s conspiracy to hollow out Indian democracy by stealing votes is coming out into the open. Instead of acting as the guardian of fair elections, the Election Commission is functioning like the “Save BJP’s Chair Commission,” he wrote on X.

Both leaders said that in West Bengal, 91% of the voter names struck off in the SIR had to be reinstated after appeals. “That means 9 out of every 10 names were wrongly deleted, and added back only after the election. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft”, Mr. Gandhi said.

Mr. Kharge said that the “same game” was being repeated in Delhi. “Voters were increased before the Assembly elections, then names of 4.756 million voters vanished from the draft list, and preparations are underway to issue notices to 3.3 million other voters,” he said.

He said that in Telangana and Karnataka, Congress workers faced similar manipulations every day. “The country is now uniting against vote theft. The nation has understood the BJP’s conspiracy, the thief has been caught. Punishment will surely be meted out for holding democracy captive,” he added.

The Election Commission, meanwhile, has shared figures showing that 3,35,910 booth-level agents appointed by different recognised political parties were engaged in preparing the draft electoral roll for Maharashtra, and another 33,226 for Delhi.

World.title: Morning Digest: U.S.-Iran hostility flares up again, PM Modi urges SCO to dismantle terror ecosystem, and more
World.content:
U.S. and Iran trade strikes as hostilities flare again

The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), and Tehran fired missiles and drones in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war that has lasted more than six months. The U.S. strikes followed others on Sunday that abruptly ended a month without military action and threatened to fully reignite a conflict that has spiked global oil prices and posed political problems for Republicans in November’s midterm congressional elections. The renewed fighting comes after President Donald Trump had appeared to pivot toward trying to bend Iran to his will through economic sanctions.

SCO must dismantle ecosystem of terror financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens: PM

The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) “must dismantle” the ecosystem of terrorism and send a strong message to countries that practise terrorism as a state policy, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) in his remarks at the 26th SCO summit in Bishkek, the capital of the Kyrgyz Republic.

Three candidates shortlisted for Ram Janmabhoomi Trust’s first CEO

The search committee constituted to select the first Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust (SRJTKT) has shortlisted three candidates and submitted their names to the Trust, the committee said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026). The Trust, which oversees the Ram temple in Ayodhya, is expected to choose one of the three candidates at a meeting on Wednesday (September 2, 2026).

Avoid ‘unfamiliar, unusual’ fish from Nepal’s flood waters, Bihar govt. advisory cautions

Against the backdrop of the devastating flash flood in Nepal, which has left hundreds dead and many more missing, the Dairy, Fisheries and Animal Resources Department of Bihar on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) issued a public advisory cautioning against the consumption of “unfamiliar and unusual” fish caught from the flood waters flowing into the State’s rivers from Nepal.

Supreme Court quashes FIRs against against Gen Z NEET-UG protesters under Article 142

The Supreme Court, on the urging of the Union government, took a rare and extraordinary step on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) to quash criminal cases registered against Gen Z protesters involved in nationwide protests linked to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) following the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak.

7,229 CBI cases under Corruption Prevention Act pending trial; 409 for over 20 years: CVC report

More than 7,200 cases probed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) under the Prevention of Corruption (PC) Act were pending trial as on December 31, 2025. Of these, more than 400 cases were pending for over 20 years, according to the annual report of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).

Mamata Banerjee’s niece found dead at home in Birbhum

The 31-year-old niece of former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee was found dead at her residence in West Bengal’s Birbhum on Tuesday (September 1, 2026). Police said she was the daughter of one of Ms. Banerjee’s maternal cousins, who was also a local Trinamool Congress leader in Birbhum’s Kusumba village under the Rampurhat police station.

Zelenskyy warns ‘safe days in Russian skies are over’

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) warned airlines, insurance firms and passengers that Russian airspace would be “completely unsafe” and filled with Ukrainian drones for the duration of the war. “Today, we want to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, and everyone who still uses Russia’s key airports: Russian airspace is becoming completely unsafe,” he said in his nightly address.

Former U.K. PM Starmer to step down as MP

Former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced that he would step down as MP and focus on “international affairs” among other areas, even as his successor, Andy Burnham, faced lawmakers for the first time in the House of Commons since ousting Mr. Starmer from office in July.

World.title: Putin seeks to end Ukraine conflict; open for talks
World.content:
President Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) that Russia was winning the war in Ukraine and portrayed the Ukrainian leadership ‌as “terrorists” with whom it was not possible for Moscow to negotiate.

Mr. Putin, in his most ‌detailed comments on the war for many weeks, ‌acknowledged ⁠that Ukrainian attacks inside Russia had inflicted ⁠real damage and said that drones posed a particular challenge.

But he said that Russia was advancing on the battlefield and told ​reporters, “I have no doubt ‌the enemy will crumble.”

He declined to say when that would happen.

Rumours that Russia would be forced to order a new military mobilisation were “utter ‌nonsense”, he said.

Russian troops had captured 270 ​square km (168 square miles) of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine in August, and ⁠a large group of Ukrainian troops were surrounded, Putin said.

Reuters could not independently verify his statement.

Russia continues ‌to advance towards the cities of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, Mr. Putin said, adding that Moscow’s forces were preparing to launch massive strikes against energy infrastructure in Ukraine.

Mr. Putin said that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s warning to airlines that Ukrainian drones would effectively shut down Russian ‌airspace sounded like “state terrorism” and that Moscow would find a ​way to respond if it happened.

Speaking at a news conference after a summit ⁠in Kyrgyzstan, Mr. Putin said it was not possible to negotiate ⁠with “terrorists”.

He also said, however, that Moscow was open to “concrete” talks on settling the Ukraine ‌conflict if new momentum could be injected.

World.title: 5 security personnel among 6 martyred in Balochistan Customs House attack, 21 terrorists killed across province: ISPR
World.content:
Five security personnel, including two officers, and a Customs official were martyred during a “coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House” on the night of August 31-September 1 in Balochistan, the military’s media wing said.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that on the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, during multiple incidents in Nokcha, Chagai District, and Ziarat Cross, Pishin District, twenty-one terrorists belonging to Indian-sponsored proxies of Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij were sent to hell due to effective responses by the Security Forces.

The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

“During the night of Aug 31-Sep 1, terrorists belonging to Fitna al- Khawarij launched a coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House.

“Security forces responded effectively and, after an intense fire exchange, killed 10 terrorists,” ISPR added.

Moreover, fleeing terrorists were also engaged by the security forces, inflicting further casualties, the ISPR said.

“During the exchange of fire, six brave sons of the soil, including two officers and a government official from the Customs Department, made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty and embraced shahadat,” it said.

The attack on the Customs House was a “manifestation of the terror-crime nexus, orchestrated to prevent Customs officials from performing their lawful duties and thereby facilitate the continuation of criminal activities in the area”, the ISPR stated.

It added that the sanitisation operations were continuing in the surrounding areas to eliminate any remaining terrorists and ensure the safety and security of the local population as well as the vital national highways.

Separately, on 31 August, terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan attempted to disrupt the peaceful movement of commuters along N-40 Quetta–Taftan Highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion, ISPR said.

“Security forces responded immediately and, after an intense fire exchange, 11 terrorists were killed on the spot.

“A large quantity of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered from the terrorists,” it added.

“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of ‘Azm-i-Istehkam,’ as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue with full resolve. Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and foreign-supported terrorism from the country,” the ISPR concluded.

On Monday, the security forces killed 12 terrorists following an attack on a convoy of vehicles from the Reko Diq copper and gold project, in the Chagai area.

On the same day, it was reported that two terrorists had also been killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Washuk district.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.08, high-speed diesel by Rs0.51
World.content:
The government on Tuesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.08 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.51 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs343.87 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.92 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on September 2 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: PM Shehbaz says water ‘lifeblood’ of region, must never be weaponised
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday said water was the “lifeblood” of the region and must never be weaponised, as he addressed a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Kyrgyzstan.

Speaking at the SCO Council of Heads of States (CHS) meeting in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek, the premier said the region cannot “realise its full potential without lasting peace”.

Without naming India directly, he highlighted the issue of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and demanded that it be honoured.

“Water is the lifeblood of our region. It sustains millions of lives, nourishes our land and secures the very future of our coming generations,” he noted.

He stressed that it “must never be weaponised; it cannot be used as an instrument of coercion, nor can it ever be exploited for political leverage”.

“The treaties governing our shared waters are solemn, binding international commitments. They are not matters of political convenience to be cast aside at your will. They must be honoured unconditionally, in both letter and spirit.”

In a later statement on X, the premier said he was honoured to address the ceremony as Pakistan assumed chairmanship of the SCO, reiterating that water “is the lifeblood of our region” and must never be weaponised by any state.

He also noted that Pakistan made “immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism”, and added that Pakistan will conduct its chairmanship of the body under the theme ‘Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity’.

“I am confident that the SCO will continue to grow from strength to strength and bring meaningful improvements to the lives of its more than 3 billion people,” he writes.

The prime minister’s speech comes a day after the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) ordered India to uphold the IWT with Pakistan and suspend work on a hydro project in occupied Kashmir.

The Hague-based court backed Pakistan’s stance, declaring that the IWT between the two countries remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement.

Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between India and Pakistan, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025.

‘Terrorism one of the gravest threats’

Speaking on the issue of terrorism, PM Shehbaz said it remained “one of the gravest threats that has affected our entire region in its various forms and manifestations”.

As chair of the SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), Pakistan has “worked actively to strengthen regional counter-terrorism cooperation”, he highlighted.

“Few nations have fought against the scourge of terrorism as resolutely and valiantly as Pakistan. In the past two and a half decades, we have sacrificed more than 90,000 lives and endured economic losses of over $150 billion in combatting terrorism.”

Pakistan sought a peaceful and stable Afghanistan, he said, adding: “But let there be no ambiguity; so long as terrorists continue to use Afghan territory to shed the blood of innocent Pakistanis and other nations, lasting peace will remain beyond our reach.”

In his speech, the prime minister also mentioned Pakistan’s mediation efforts in the US-Iran war and laid out the country’s plan as it assumed the SCO CHS chair.

PM Shehbaz was welcomed by the Kyrgyz president upon his arrival at the summit’s venue on Tuesday, and later posed with other world leaders for a group photo.

Leaders from China, Iran, Turkiye, Russia, and India were also in Kyrgyzstan for the two-day summit. The regional bloc, which also includes Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Belarus, is celebrating its 25th anniversary.

A video clip shared by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) showed PM Shehbaz speaking to China’s President Xi Jinping. He could also be seen sitting together with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

The premier also held informal meetings with the presidents of Iran, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Belarus.

Taking SCO chair, Pakistan proposes ‘excellent plan’

Pakistan has assumed the chairmanship of the SCO CHS for 2026–27, with next year’s summit to be hosted by Islamabad.

“As Pakistan assumes the chairmanship of the SCO, we are proposing an excellent plan that will prioritise key sectors, including IT and AI, energy development, poverty reduction, disaster management, health, culture and sports,” PM Shehbaz said during his address.

As part of that plan, Pakistan proposed establishing an SCO framework for sovereign AI infrastructure and governance to “promote responsible and inclusive AI development and to also ensure that no member state is left behind”.

The prime minister said Pakistan’s SCO chairmanship will be pursued under the theme, ‘Turning vision into action, connectivity, innovation and shared prosperity’.

“We undertake this responsibility with humility, hope and abiding faith that connectivity will bring our peoples closer, innovation will open new doors of opportunity, and shared prosperity will reach every home,” the premier said.

He called for turning the SCO vision into action and its promises into progress.

PM Shehbaz said: “Let us […] move forward together with the resolve that, in a time of uncertainty, history will record the SCO as having chosen cooperation over confrontation, dialogue over division, and hope over fear.

“Let history record that the SCO did not merely witness a changing world; we shaped it together.”

The premier noted that the SCO region was inhabited by over 3bn people and blessed with abundant natural resources. “This extraordinary potential also places upon us SCO leaders an extraordinary responsibility to shape a better future for our peoples.”

He recalled that he has long advocated for regional connectivity as the “key to our prosperity”.

“Today, connectivity is no longer a choice; it is a strategic imperative. The regional crisis has also proven that diversified transport networks, secure energy corridors and resilient supply chains are indispensable to our collective security.”

PM Shehbaz said the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) continued to “serve as a gateway, linking the regional economies to the Arabian Sea”.

He affirmed that Islamabad remained committed to advancing existing trans-regional railway projects, road connectivity initiatives and regional energy projects.

The prime minister called for ensuring the implementation of the SCO Development Strategy until 2035, adding that the establishment of the SCO Development Bank would be a “critical step” in this regard.

As the permanent chair of the Special Working Group of the SCO on Poverty Reduction, Pakistan will continue to strengthen social protection and promote inclusive and sustainable development across the SCO region, he pledged.

‘Intensifying geopolitical tensions’

The premier noted that today’s global landscape “is marked by intensifying geopolitical tensions, fragmenting global economy, escalating climate crises and unprecedented technological transformation”.

“In such a complex environment, the SCO represents our collective resolve to navigate through these enormous challenges together and deliver peace, security and prosperity to our peoples,” he observed.

The prime minister affirmed that Pakistan “consistently upholds and respects the core principles of both the UN and SCO charters”.

“We remain committed to resolving disputes peacefully through international law, adhering strictly to the guidelines of the SCO charter.”

He highlighted that in line with this spirit, Islamabad “staunchly advocated peace when the sovereignty and territorial integrity of an SCO member state was violated earlier this year, triggering a major regional crisis”.

PM Shehbaz then noted that Pakistan and the international community have “borne a heavy economic cost” as the “closure of critical energy supply routes” disrupted the global economy, referring to the Strait of Hormuz.

“In these challenging times, Pakistan has consistently acted as an honest and sincere mediator and facilitator,” he affirmed.

He recalled that Islamabad’s “sustained diplomatic efforts culminated in the signing of the landmark Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding” in June, terming the document a “critical step towards regional de-escalation and the restoration of peace”.

The premier noted that peace-building efforts were continuing and extended his “deepest gratitude to the brotherly and friendly countries, many of whom are represented here today, for their unwavering support throughout this endeavour”.

“We firmly believe that the Islamabad MoU offers the most viable and enduring pathway to lasting peace in the region.”

The 14-point MoU, signed in June, provided a framework for ending the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. It was a result of mediation efforts spearheaded by Pakistan and others.

Besides signing the Islamabad MoU as the mediator, Pakistan had also brokered a ceasefire between the US and Iran in April.

The April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks, mainly around the Strait of Hormuz, have dimmed the prospects of a final peace agreement.

At the SCO summit, the prime minister also mentioned the signing of the trilateral defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month, named the “Makkah Defence Alliance”.

He reiterated that the pact was “fundamentally defensive in nature and is neither directed against any state nor intended to create any confrontation or division whatsoever”.

He emphasised that while Pakistan has always strived to strengthen multilateralism, “multilateral organisations must be empowered to translate aspirations into action”.

“The plight of the innocent people of Gaza and West Bank continues unabated, causing unimaginable suffering. Palestinian mothers endure the profound grief of mourning their children, families remain torn apart, and entire generations continue to live under a perpetual shadow of fear, deprivation and gross injustice.”

The premier called upon the international community to honour its commitment to “help the Palestinian people, alongside all other oppressed nations, secure their fundamental right to self-determination”.

On Monday, Israeli airstrikes killed five people around Gaza City, a local hospital and rescuers said. Despite a US-backed ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, violence has not halted in the Gaza Strip, with Israel continuing to target Palestinians it claims are fighters.

At the outset of his speech, PM Shehbaz congratulated the Kyrgyz Republic on the completion of its “successful SCO chairmanship and for making impressive contributions to further advance practical cooperation among the SCO members”.

The prime minister also felicitated the leadership and people of Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan for their respective independence days.

The premier described the gathering as “historic” and extended his gratitude to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Nurgozhoevich Japarov and his team for their hospitality and “excellent arrangements” made for the summit.

“Guided by the Shanghai spirit, Pakistan takes great pride in being part of the SCO, as we celebrate 25 years of this remarkable journey, a milestone for which I congratulate all fellow members,” PM Shehbaz told the summit.

“From a tender sapling, the SCO has grown into a towering tree, providing the shade of security and stability for all of us.”

Lahore named SCO’s Tourism and Culture Capital for 2026-27

The city of Lahore has been named the Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27 by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).

The title of Tourism and Cultural Capital has been rotated annually among SCO member states since 2022, and the designation serves to highlight the prominence of a city that embodies the cultural heritage of the country that takes over the rotating presidency of the organisation.

The designation is designed to promote people-to-people contacts and tourism among the member states.

Cities that have held the title in the past include Varanasi, India (2022-23), Almaty, Kazakhstan (2023-24), Qingdao, China (2024-25) and Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan (2025-26).

The decision to designate Lahore as the tourism and cultural capital was taken in April this year, when the heads of tourism administrations of SCO member states met in Bishkek.

UN urgently in need of reform, PM tells SCO Plus summit

PM Shehbaz also addressed the SCO Plus summit, an expanded format of the regional bloc.

The prime minister noted that the United Nations was established to “fulfil the universal dream of ending all wars and building enduring peace”.

Stressing that Pakistan has remained fully committed to the UN Charter in the past eight decades, he said: “We see the rise of a multipolar world as an opportunity to build a more equitable, democratic and just international system.

“But today, the UN is urgently in need of reform. It must become more accountable and responsive.”

As a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council, Pakistan has been “actively contributing to global peacemaking over the past two years”, PM Shehbaz highlighted.

He noted that these efforts culminated in the signing of the Islamabad MoU, stressing that it offers a “widely accepted basis for all parties to pursue peace through dialogue and diplomacy”.

Speaking about the Makkah defence pact, PM Shehbaz said the agreement “has further strengthened the prospect for peace in the region by sending a message of unity and common resolve, as well as to promote progress and prosperity in the region”.

He reiterated his concerns over the situation in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, terming it “deeply troubling”. The premier demanded that the international community “act decisively and now to end the suffering of innocent Palestinian people and uphold their inalienable right to self-determination”.

“The same rights must also be granted to all other oppressed nations around the globe.”

The premier reiterated his remarks about the water issue in his address to the SCO Plus Summit.

Speaking on terrorism, he affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to battling the “three evils of terrorism: separatism, terrorism and religious extremism” under the SCO’s RATS.

“We believe that terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, including state terrorism, must be condemned in clear and unambiguous terms,” he asserted.

The prime minister stressed the need for the SCO to “deliver tangible dividends to its peoples”.

“I reaffirm Pakistan’s solemn resolve and commitment to realise the true potential of the SCO. In our efforts to elevate the SCO to even greater heights, we seek the kind cooperation of SCO member states, as well as our valued SCO Plus family.”

He then invited the participants to the next edition of the SCO Plus summit set to be held in Islamabad.

The government later said that PM Shehbaz met UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the summit.

PM pledges to boost cooperation with Belarus

On the sidelines of the summit, PM Shehbaz met Belarusian President Aleksandr Lukashenko, and both leaders expressed satisfaction with the positive trajectory of bilateral ties and cooperation across the political, trade, and economic spheres, among others.

In a statement posted on X, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said that both leaders pledged to boost cooperation in trade, industry, agriculture, IT and vocational training as priority sectors, with PM Shehbaz extending an invitation to Lukashenko to once again visit Pakistan.

Lukashenko visited Pakistan in 2024, with PM Shehbaz visiting Belarus last year.

“Both leaders reaffirmed their shared commitment and resolve to elevate the long-standing friendly relations between Pakistan and Belarus to new heights,” the statement read.

Lahore named SCO’s Tourism and Culture Capital for 2026-27

The city of Lahore has been named the Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27 by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).

The title of Tourism and Cultural Capital has been rotated annually among SCO member states since 2022, and the designation serves to highlight the prominence of a city that embodies the cultural heritage of the country that takes over the rotating presidency of the organisation.

The designation is designed to promote people-to-people contacts and tourism among the member states.

Cities that have held the title in the past include Varanasi, India (2022-23), Almaty, Kazakhstan (2023-24), Qingdao, China (2024-25) and Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan (2025-26).

The decision to designate Lahore as the tourism and cultural capital was taken in April this year, when the heads of tourism administrations of SCO member states met in Bishkek.

Dar meets counterparts from Iran, China, others

On the sidelines of the twin SCO summits, DPM Dar interacted with the foreign ministers of China, Russia, Iran, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Belarus and Armenia, among other leaders.

The Foreign Office (FO) shared pictures of Dar, Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi, Russian FM Sergey Lavrov, Tajik FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin and Kazakh FM Yermek Kosherbayev having a “warm and cordial interaction”.

Earlier in the day, Dar, who arrived in Bishkek a day ago to join PM Shehbaz, had a “warm exchange” with Iran’s Araghchi.

Dar stressed that the “sincere implementation” of the Islamabad MoU was the only way forward amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, according to FO.

Describing the meeting as a “warm exchange”, FO said the two ministers exchanged views on bilateral relations and regional developments and reaffirmed the importance of continued engagement.

“The DPM underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain essential to promoting peace and stability in the region, and that sincere implementation by both parties to the conflict of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding of June 2026 remains the only way forward,” FO said in a statement on X.

A day ago, PM Shehbaz had met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the summit in Bishkek and underscored the need to build on the understandings reached under the Islamabad MoU.

Dar “held a warm and cordial exchange” with China’s FM Wang Yi, FO said. Both leaders reaffirmed the All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership between Pakistan and China.

They also discussed matters of mutual interest, including the upcoming United Nations General Assembly session this month in New York and the ongoing process for the election of the next UN secretary-general.

DPM Dar also met with the director of Türkiye’s National Intelligence Organisation (MİT), İbrahim Kalın.

“The two sides exchanged views on regional developments and matters of mutual interest, including the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the inaugural meeting of its Strategic Political and Defence Committee, as well as recent developments in the region,” FO said.

Dar underscored the importance of continued coordination and diplomatic engagement for regional peace, security and stability.

The deputy premier and his Russian counterpart Alexei Overchuk had a “productive exchange of views on bilateral relations”, FO said.

They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the close Pakistan–Russia partnership, enhancing cooperation, and maintaining high-level engagement between the two sides. They also discussed regional and international developments of mutual interest.

World.title: Afghan-origin doctor, policeman among eight held; meth worth Rs900m seized
World.content:
KARACHI: A police task force on narcotics in Karachi, in collaboration with a federal civilian intelligence agency, carried out an intelligence-based raid on a warehouse in Mehran Town, Korangi, on Tuesday, arresting eight members of an alleged “international narcotics network” and recovering 50kg of crystal meth, also known as ice, worth Rs900 million.

Speaking at a press conference, West Deputy Inspector General of Police Irfan Ali Baloch said the suspects were allegedly operating an international narcotics network and transporting drugs from Pakistan to Thailand and Malaysia in bulk quantities.

He said the police had recovered 50kg of ice, estimated to be worth Rs900 million. He revealed that the consignment intercepted before export weighed between 200kg and 250kg and had an estimated value of $25 million to $30m (Rs6 billion to Rs8bn). He added that more consignments were expected to arrive in Karachi from Balochistan.

“Acting on credible information, the task force, in conjunction with the intelligence agency, established that the narcotics were being concealed in crates of tiles and marble at a warehouse in Mehran Town for export to the Philippines under the cover of a ‘legitimate’ consignment,” DIG Baloch said.

“A covert operation was mounted against an international network trafficking methamphetamine (ice) to Malaysia and the Philippines.”

Sharing details of the trafficking routes and the network’s linkages, DIG Baloch said the present consignment was destined for the Philippines from Karachi, with overseas handlers in South Africa and Thailand.

He said the network had established links in Karachi, while the ice was sourced from Chaman in Balochistan and hawala transactions were routed through Lahore.

Regarding the roles of the eight suspects, DIG Baloch said Nazir Soomro was the principal accused who directed the procurement, concealment and export of the consignment.

He added that Shahid Mastoi arranged and maintained the Mehran Town warehouse used to conceal the narcotics, while Sheikh Khalid provided storage for the drugs and facilitated banking channels for local transactions.

According to the DIG, Dr Noor Ahmed Khilji and Garan Khan, both of Afghan origin and holders of Pakistani CNICs, arranged the supply from Balochistan.

Abdullah alias Wahab worked as a courier, while Mohammed Kamran, also a courier, was a police constable posted in Malir. Nasir worked as an intermediary and distributor, facilitating transactions involving Dr Noor.

He said the police recovered 50kg of ice, along with a car, two pistols and Rs350,000, from the suspects.

The DIG said the ice was procured locally at Rs220,000 per kilogram and contracted for export at $6,000 per kilogram, against an estimated destination-market price of $100,000 to $120,000 per kilogram.

Of the 200kg to 250kg contracted for export, the remaining quantity had not been delivered, he said, adding that the full consignment had an estimated destination-market value of $25 million to $30m (Rs6bn to Rs8bn).

Organised network

DIG Baloch said the case pointed to an “organised network” with domestic and international linkages involving procurement, financing, concealment and attempted export.

He said the concealment of the narcotics in a commercial consignment of marble indicated the “deliberate exploitation of legitimate trade channels”.

“Overseas handlers, suppliers, financial facilitators, warehouse operators and clearing agents indicate a structured supply chain, not an isolated attempt,” the senior officer said.

He feared that had the consignment reached its destination, it could have caused reputational damage to Pakistan internationally.

Tracing foreign linkages

DIG Baloch said the narcotics task force, which also included the Special Investigation Unit (SIU), was further questioning the arrested suspects to establish the full network, identify additional facilitators and beneficiaries, and trace the complete financial trail, including the cryptocurrency advance and local accounts used in the transactions.

He added that the task force was also verifying the identities and roles of foreign handlers in Malaysia, Thailand and South Africa in coordination with other law-enforcement agencies, customs authorities and international counterparts to trace the network’s overseas linkages.

World.title: UK vows anti-settler measures as Israel warns of retaliation
World.content:
Britain’s foreign secretary vowed a tough response to “appalling” violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, drawing threats from Israel that it would retaliate if the UK imposed sanctions.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing allies have been ramping up support for settlements in the run-up to close-fought elections, despite increasing attacks by extremist settlers who seek to drive out Palestinians.

But the issue has drawn mounting criticism from foreign governments, many of which had already seen their ties with Israel strained over its conduct of the Gaza war.

Speaking in parliament on Tuesday, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the world had “seen appalling settler terrorism and Palestinians driven from their homes”, and vowed a “comprehensive reset of our policy”.

“This government will not acquiesce in the destruction of the two-state solution. We will act, and I will set out a comprehensive set of measures in the coming weeks,” Miliband said.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar later told a podcast: “If Britain acts against the State of Israel, the State of Israel will act against Britain.”

Saar did not explain how Israel would retaliate against Britain, a veto-wielding member of the UN Security Council and the world’s fifth-largest economy, but it has reportedly looked at expelling diplomats.

“The era in which it was possible to act against the State of Israel and the State of Israel did not respond is over. If they act, I think they will be making a big mistake,” Saar said, also accusing London of “meddling” in the October 27 election.

Hardening UK stance

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said that his predecessor Keir Starmer was too soft on Israel, which has come under intense international criticism over its relentless offensive that flattened much of Gaza in response to the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, the worst ever against Israel.

Starmer’s government did, however, announce sanctions in June on six entities and one person “involved in financing, enabling and carrying out settler violence” as part of a set of measures in coordination with a handful of other Western countries.

Miliband on Tuesday called the so-called E1 development plan — under which more than 1,200 settler homes were greenlit by Israel last year — “the crossing of a red line, as it cuts through the heart of the West Bank and risks making a Palestinian state unviable”.

Israel recently went ahead with tenders for the project, which has long been opposed by the Palestinians as it would divide the West Bank’s north and the south.

Buildings in the Israeli settlement of Har Bracha (Brakha) are pictured in the background as an Israeli military excavator demolishes a Palestinian building on the outskirts of Nablus in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on August 31, 2026. — AFP

Miliband, the son of Jewish refugees, said that Britain was looking at “our wider economic relationship with the occupied territories”.

“We do not want British companies financing, constructing or advertising new settlements,” he said.

Israel has fought against foreign governments making any distinction between goods from Israel and West Bank settlements, which are considered illegal under international law.

Israel recently expelled two Dutch diplomats from a US-led centre in charge of coordinating a fledgling Gaza ceasefire after the Netherlands, traditionally one of Europe’s more pro-Israeli countries, banned trade from settlements.

The British embassy in Israel afterwards said that it was participating in the centre at the request of the United States and to support the Gaza peace plan, and that removing it would “undermine these joint efforts”.

Rising violence

More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967, alongside three million Palestinians.

Extremist Israeli settlers, many of whom believe in a biblical right to the territory, have been carrying out increasingly brazen attacks against Palestinians, including seizing their land and destroying their crops.

In one of the latest incidents, settlers on Tuesday tried to set fire to a mosque in the northern West Bank, in what the Palestinian ministry of religious affairs said was the 13th such desecration of a mosque this year.

A man stands by graffiti in Hebrew left by Israeli settlers following a reported arson attack on a mosque in the Palestinian village of Bazzaryah, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on September 1, 2026. — AFP

The settlers left graffiti with threatening messages in Hebrew and criticism of the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, AFP pictures showed.

Israel has long enjoyed robust support from the United States and Huckabee, an evangelical pastor, has long championed settlements.

But Huckabee issued rare criticism and described a group of settlers as “terrorists” after they tried to cut off Palestinian homes in Qusra, including one belonging to a US citizen.

World.title: Mir Raza murder case: Judicial commission records statements, MLO says he was ‘under no pressure’ during autopsy
World.content:
KARACHI: The judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances surrounding the murder of Mir Raza Ali and possible negligence in the case on Tuesday recorded the testimonies of a medico-legal officer (MLO), police officials, two volunteers of a charity organisation, gardeners and members of the aggrieved family.

The one-member commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, also summoned several other individuals, including the victim’s business partner, friends and police officials, to appear before it on Sept 3.

The provincial government formed the judicial commission to probe the circumstances leading to the death of young entrepreneur Mir Raza, determine whether there was any negligence on the part of medical and police officials during the investigation, and make recommendations for further investigation, forensic analysis or legal and departmental action.

Medico-legal officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted the first autopsy, appeared before the commission and said he had not been under any influence or pressure and had not mentioned suicide in his report.

He also deposed that, after completing his MBBS in 2016, he was appointed through the Sindh Public Service Commission in 2019. He joined the police surgeon’s office in 2021 and was posted as an MLO at Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre.

Responding to a question from the commission, Dr Sheikh said he had so far conducted around 100 post-mortems. He added that a sweeper used to be present during such procedures.

Justice Sial also asked why burn marks on the deceased’s hands and other parts of the body, as well as fractures, had not been mentioned in his report. Dr Sheikh replied that there were no burn marks and that the change in the skin’s colour was due to decomposition. He also said he had found no visible fractures.

The commission expressed serious displeasure over the MLO’s failure to provide satisfactory answers, questioning how the body had decomposed so quickly and why he had been able to identify only a bullet wound during the entire procedure.

Justice Sial further asked the MLO whether the autopsy had been conducted by the sweeper. He also pointed out that the final report of the first autopsy differed from the initial report and that the handwriting in the two reports did not match.

The MLO maintained that he had conducted the autopsy and acknowledged that the handwriting in both reports was his. He explained that the final report of the first post-mortem was issued after the body had been exhumed and a second autopsy conducted, as well as after the police surgeon had raised 14 objections to the first post-mortem.

He also maintained that he had prepared the initial autopsy report without any influence or pressure and had not mentioned suicide in it.

“On Aug 9, I was called to the Chief Minister’s House, where DIG Farrukh Ali Lanjar asked me to record a statement or provide information about the case. However, I refused to do so in the absence of the relevant documents,” it said.

The MLO further told the commission that the second investigation team had recorded his statement on Aug 17. He added that the body was around 24 to 36 hours old and that anaesthetics had been detected in the blood.

The two nursery employees, Yasir and Qaiser, who had informed the police about the body, deposed that they called the police helpline (15) shortly after spotting it. They said two policemen arrived on a motorcycle about 15 minutes later, followed by a police van.

They also told the commission that the police recorded their statements under Section 161 of the CrPC three days later. The employees added that police officers used to be present at the nursery’s main entrance for around 20 days a month.

Two Edhi Foundation volunteers, Mohsin and Javed, also appeared before the commission and testified that they had reached the site at around 1pm after receiving information about the body from their head office.

They said that upon reaching the scene, they found the body lying face down. After turning it over, they noticed a bullet wound on the victim’s body.

Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Nadeem Mughal told the commission that he was performing his duties at Gulistan-i-Jauhar police station when he was directed to proceed to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC).

“I handed over the samples collected during the autopsy to the SIO of Ferozabad police station, Shabbir Laghari,” he added.

ASI Azhar Abbas, who was also posted at Gulistan-i-Jauhar police station, said he shared pictures of the body with the SHO and duty officer after reaching the crime scene.

Another policeman, Mohammad Arif, said he was a device operator for the Talash (search) app and had attempted to record the victim’s fingerprints, but could not do so because of the decomposition.

The victim’s parents, Mir Hussain Ali Khan and Mariam Hussain, and his sister, Alishba Khan, were also present during the hearing along with their lawyer, Jibran Nasir. They provided further details about the incident.

The case

The case has been mired in controversy since the beginning. While Ali’s family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had initially built the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

Days after the recovery of Ali’s body, Dr Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir, accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8.

A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered.

The order for the probe team’s reconstitution also showed that a murder charge had been added to the first information report.

The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team.

On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation”. They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved.

The provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced the decision on Aug 23 to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ali’s death.

However, soon after the announcement, the counsel for Ali’s family raised objections and later approached the Sindh High Court (SHC).

The petition was filed on August 24 in objection to the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission and sought the formation of an independent and multi-agency JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case” in place of the commission.

The commission held the first hearing on Friday and summoned MLO Sheikh. It had also issued notices to the deceased’s family, their lawyer and a provincial government focal person.

World.title: Punjab Assembly passes resolution seeking ban on social media for under-16s
World.content:
LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday passed a resolution seeking an effective legal ban on social media accounts for children under 16 years of age.

The resolution was submitted to the Punjab Assembly in July by the chairperson of the Child Protection Bureau, Sarah Ahmad. It called for effective legislation and a coordinated mechanism between federal and provincial institutions to protect minors from the growing dangers of social media.

The resolution noted that social media use was exposing children to cyberbullying, online sexual exploitation, inappropriate content, mental stress and other serious risks.

It referred to measures introduced in Australia, France, China and several states of the United States to regulate social media use by underage children, and urged the government to introduce similar effective legal safeguards in Pakistan.

The proposal comes at a time when governments around the world are considering stricter regulation of children’s use of social media amid mounting evidence linking excessive online activity with mental health issues, cyber abuse and exposure to harmful content.

Several countries, including Australia, besides the EU have recently moved towards imposing age-based restrictions on access to social media platforms, while others are examining stronger age-verification requirements and enhanced child online safety laws.

If adopted by the Punjab Assembly, the resolution will serve as a recommendation to the federal government, which has legislative authority over telecommunications, internet regulation and digital platforms.

Meanwhile, the House also adopted a resolution seeking equal religious education facilities and examination opportunities for prisoners belonging to minority communities.

The resolution, moved by Treasury member Raheela Khadim and adopted by majority vote, pointed out that under Rule 215 of the Punjab Prison Rules, 1978, prisoners could receive remission in their sentences for acquiring religious education in accordance with the law.

According to official data cited, 2,558 Muslim prisoners benefited from the facility after obtaining religious education between 2020 and 2025. The resolution stressed the need for effective implementation of a similar system for minority prisoners.

It demanded that Christian, Hindu, Sikh and prisoners belonging to other minority faiths should be given equal opportunities to study their respective religious curricula, appear in examinations and receive sentence remission upon successfully completing religious education, as provided under the law.

World.title: Bank of America VP among two killed in stabbing in New York's Times Square; suspect shot dead
World.content:
A knife-wielding woman stabbed and killed two people in New York’s tourist-filled Times Square on Monday, before she was shot and killed by police.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the deaths in a press conference, saying that the second victim was in stable condition in a hospital.

The attacker, identified as 49-year-old Queens resident Pamela Cisneros, who was known to have mental health issues, pulled two large knives from a bag bearing the logo of a well-known supermarket chain before threatening passersby in broad daylight, New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said.

She then approached a 68-year-old man and stabbed him in the abdomen. Twenty seconds later, she attacked a 32-year-old woman, also stabbing her in the abdomen — wounds to which she later succumbed.

The second victim, Erin Piacenti, was Vice President of Bank of America’s business selection and conflicts unit, according to her LinkedIn profile.

“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,” the US banking giant said in an emailed statement to Reuters on Tuesday.

Police quickly intervened and tried to persuade Cisneros to drop her weapons.

“The officers engaged the woman in dialogue for four minutes and gave her numerous commands to drop the knives, which she refused,” Tisch said.

“During the encounter, she told the officers, ‘I’m not dropping anything. I would rather kill both of you,’” Tisch added.

One witness told local TV outlet PIX11 that the suspect had two knives in her hands and was tased by police before she rushed at officers.

“They shot her twice,” said the unnamed witness.

Police confirmed that they had unsuccessfully used a stun gun before firing their handguns.

The scene of an officer-involved shooting, in Times Square, New York City, US on August 31, 2026. — Reuters

Local news reports said the suspect was pronounced dead at the hospital. Tisch said that they do not believe the attack was terror-related.

“This was an extraordinarily dangerous situation unfolding in the heart of Times Square, the crossroads of the world,” the police chief said.

“At any given moment, there are 1,000s of New Yorkers, commuters, tourists, families, workers moving through these streets.”

An AFP journalist at the scene saw a large emergency services presence and officials inspecting a patch of blood in Times Square.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
